The second: His saying ﴿and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾ is restricted to the removal of Hellfire, while His saying ﴿and protect them from evil deeds﴾ encompasses the punishment of Hellfire, the punishment of the standing place of the Resurrection, and the punishment of the reckoning and questioning.

The second opinion regarding His saying, ﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾, is that the angels asked for the removal of the punishment of the Fire by saying, ﴿And protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, and they asked for the bringing of the reward of Paradise to them by saying, ﴿And admit them to gardens of perpetual residence﴾. Then, after that, they asked that Allah, exalted is He, safeguard them in this world from corrupt beliefs and corrupt deeds, and this is what is meant by their saying, ﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾. Then they said, ﴿And whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day, You have certainly had mercy on him﴾, meaning: whoever You protect from evil deeds in this world, You have certainly had mercy on him on the Day of Resurrection. Then they said, ﴿That is the great success﴾, since they found, through temporary deeds, a bliss that never ends, and through humble deeds, a dominion whose true greatness the intellects cannot reach.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 40, verse 7–9 (part 1 of 3):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise, and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire."﴾ ﴿"Our Lord, and admit them into the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise."﴾ ﴿"And protect them from evil deeds. Whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have indeed shown them mercy. That is the great triumph."﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, explained that the disbelievers exaggerate in displaying enmity towards the believers, He explained that the noblest of the classes of created beings are the angels who are the bearers of the Throne, and those who surround the Throne, who exaggerate in displaying love and support for the believers. It is as if He, exalted is He, says: If these lowly ones exaggerate in enmity, then do not care for them, do not turn to them, and do not give them any weight, for the bearers of the Throne are with you, and those around the Throne are with you, supporting you. There are several issues concerning the verse:

The first issue: He, exalted is He, related this account concerning two kinds of groups of angels:

The first category: ﴿those who bear the Throne﴾. Exalted is He has related that those who bear the Throne on the Day of Resurrection are eight. It may be said: those who bear it at this time are those same eight who will bear it on the Day of Resurrection. And there is no doubt that the bearers of the Throne are the noblest and greatest of the angels. Ṣāḥib al-Kashshāf (al-Zamakhshari) related that the feet of the bearers of the Throne are in the lowest earth and their heads have pierced the Throne, and they are in humble submission, not raising their gaze. And from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not reflect upon the greatness of your Lord, but reflect upon what Allah, exalted is He, has created of the angels, for indeed there is a created angel called Israfil, whose corner of the Throne is upon his shoulder, and his feet are in the lowest earth, and his head has passed through seven heavens, and he shrinks from the greatness of Allah until he becomes like a small thing." It was said: he is a small bird. It has also been narrated that Allah commanded all the angels to greet the bearers of the Throne with peace morning and evening, as a preference for them over the rest of the angels. It was also said: Allah created the Throne from a green jewel, and between two of its legs the flapping of a swiftly flying bird lasts eighty thousand years. It was also said: around the Throne are seventy thousand rows of angels circling it, glorifying and magnifying, and behind them are seventy thousand rows standing with their hands placed upon their shoulders, raising their voices in tahlil and takbir, and behind them are a hundred thousand rows with their right hands placed upon their left. There is not one of them but glorifies with something other than what the other glorifies. I have transmitted these reports from al-Kashshaf.

As for the second category of angels mentioned by Allah in this verse, it is His saying: ﴿and those around it﴾. The more apparent meaning is that what is meant by them is what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord with praise.﴾

I say: Reason indicates that the bearers of the Throne and those surrounding the Throne must be the best of the angels. That is because the relation of spirits to spirits is like the relation of bodies to bodies. So when the Throne was the noblest of corporeal existents, the spirits attached to governing the Throne must be better than the spirits governing bodies. Also, it is likely that there are spirits bearing the body of the Throne, and from those dominant, elevated spirits bearing the body of the Throne there come forth other spirits of their kind, attached to the edges of the Throne, and to them refers His saying: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne.﴾ In sum, it has become clear by certain proofs and by true unveilings that there is no comparison between the world of bodies and the world of spirits. So whatever you witness with the eye of sight in the varying ranks of the world of bodies, you must witness with the eye of insight in the varying ranks of the world of spirits.

The second issue: This verse indicates that He, glorified is He, is far above being in the Throne. That is because He, exalted is He, said in this verse: ﴿those who bear the Throne﴾, and He said in another verse: ﴿And above them on that Day eight will bear the Throne of your Lord﴾ [al-Haqqah: 17]. There is no doubt that the bearer of the Throne is a bearer of everything in the Throne. So if the God of the world were in the Throne, these angels would be bearing the God of the world, and then they would be guarding the God of the world. The guardian, being capable, is more deserving of divinity, and the one borne and guarded is more deserving of servitude. Then the god would become a servant and the servant a god, and that is corrupt. This shows that the God of the Throne and of bodies is exalted above the Throne and bodies.

* * *

Know that He, exalted is He, related three things concerning the bearers of the Throne and those surrounding the Throne:

The first type is His saying: ﴿they glorify their Lord with praise﴾. Its parallel is His saying, relating about the angels: ﴿while we glorify You with Your praise﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30], and His saying: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord with praise.﴾ Thus tasbih is an expression for declaring Allah far above what is unfitting, and tahmid is acknowledging that He is the absolute Bestower of blessings. So tasbih points to majesty (jalal) and tahmid points to generosity (ikram). Thus His saying ﴿they glorify their Lord with praise﴾ is close to His saying: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾ [al-Rahman: 78].

The second type of what Allah related about these angels is His saying: ﴿and they believe in Him.﴾ If it is asked: what is the benefit of His saying ﴿and they believe in Him﴾, since occupation with glorification and praise is not possible unless faith in Allah has already preceded? We say: the benefit in it is what Ṣāḥib al-Kashshāf mentioned, and he did very well in it. He said: the purpose of it is to alert that if Allah were present in the Throne, the bearers of the Throne and those surrounding the Throne would be seeing Him and witnessing Him. And since their belief in the existence of Allah entails praise and commendation, because affirming the existence of a present, seen, witnessed thing does not entail praise and commendation (do you not see that affirming the existence of the sun and that it is luminous does not entail praise and commendation?), when Allah mentioned their belief in Him in the manner of praise, commendation and exaltation, it became known that they believed in Him, as evidenced by the fact that they did not see Him present and sitting there. May Allah have mercy on Ṣāḥib al-Kashshāf; had he not included in his book anything but this point, it would have sufficed him as pride and honour.

The third type of what Allah related about these angels is His saying: ﴿and they ask forgiveness for those who believe.﴾ Know that it is established that complete happiness is tied to two matters: exalting the command of Allah, and compassion toward the creation of Allah. And it is necessary that exalting the command of Allah be prior to compassion toward the creation of Allah. So His saying ﴿they glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him﴾ indicates exalting the command of Allah, and His saying
صفحة ٣٠
﴿and they ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾ indicates compassion toward the creation of Allah.

Then there are several issues in the verse:

The first issue: Many scholars have used this verse to establish that the angel is better than the human. They said: this verse indicates that when the angels finished mentioning Allah with praise and sanctification, they occupied themselves with seeking forgiveness for others, namely the believers. This shows that they are independent of seeking forgiveness for themselves; for if they were in need of it, they would have put seeking forgiveness for themselves before seeking forgiveness for others, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Begin with yourself." Also Allah said to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So know that there is no god but Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women﴾ [Muhammad: 19]; so He commanded Muhammad to mention first seeking forgiveness for himself, and after that to seek forgiveness for others. And He related of Nuh, peace be upon him, that he said: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house believing, and the believing men and believing women﴾ [Nuh: 28]. This indicates that everyone who is in need of forgiveness puts seeking forgiveness for himself before seeking it for others. So if the angels were in need of forgiveness, their occupation with seeking forgiveness for themselves would have preceded their occupation with seeking it for others. And since Allah did not mention from them their seeking forgiveness for themselves, we know that this was because they were not in need of forgiveness. As for the prophets, peace be upon them, they were in need of forgiveness, based on His saying to Muhammad, peace be upon him: ﴿and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. And if this is established, then it is clear that the angel is better than the human. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: al-Ka'bi used this verse to establish that the effect of intercession is in the increase of reward for believers, not in removing punishment from sinners. He said: that is because the angels said: ﴿So forgive those who repent and follow Your way﴾. He said: what is meant is not "forgive those who repented from disbelief," whether he was persisting in sin or not, because one whose state is such is not described as following the way of his Lord, and that is not applied to him. Also the angels say: ﴿and admit them into the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them﴾, and this is not fitting for the wicked, because our opponents do not affirm with certainty that Allah promised them Paradise; they only permit that. So it is established that the intercession of the angels only reaches the people of obedience, and so the intercession of the prophets must be the same, since there is no one who makes a distinction. The answer: we say this verse indicates the occurrence of intercession from the angels for sinners. We will explain this, then answer what al-Ka'bi mentioned. As for the explanation of how this verse indicates what we have said, it is from several aspects:

The first: His saying: ﴿and they ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾. Seeking forgiveness is requesting forgiveness, and forgiveness is only mentioned in the removal of punishment. As for requesting an additional benefit, it is not called seeking forgiveness.

The second: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾, and this indicates that they seek forgiveness for every people of faith. So when we establish that the person who commits a major sin is a believer, it is necessary that he enter under this intercession.

The third: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So forgive those who repent﴾. Requesting forgiveness for those who repent: it is not permissible that what is meant is the removal of punishment for a major sin after repentance, because that is obligatory upon Allah according to the opponent, and what is obligatory in action, asking for it by supplication is ugly. Nor is it permissible that what is meant is the removal of punishment for minor sins, because that too is obligatory, so asking for it by supplication is not fitting. Nor is it permissible that what is meant is requesting an increase in benefit beyond the reward, because that is not called forgiveness. So it is established that His saying ﴿So forgive those who repent﴾ cannot be understood except as the removal of the punishment for a major sin before repentance. And if this is established regarding the angels, then likewise regarding the prophets, since consensus is established that there is no difference. As for what al-Ka'bi relies on, namely that they requested forgiveness for those who repented, we say: it must be that what is meant by it is those who repented from disbelief and followed the way of faith. As for his saying that one who repents from disbelief while persisting in wickedness is not called a penitent nor one who follows the way of Allah, we say: we do not concede his statement; rather it is said: he is a penitent from disbelief and a follower of the way of Allah in religion and law. And when it is established that he is a penitent from disbelief, it is established that he is a penitent. Do you not see that for the truth of describing someone as a striker or a laugher, it suffices that striking or laughing proceeds from him once, and that does not depend on all kinds of striking or laughing proceeding from him? So likewise here.

**Third issue:** The people of verification (*ahl al-tahqiq*) said: This intercession by the angels on behalf of humankind takes the form of an apology for a past lapse. When the angels first learned of the creation of humans, they said: ﴿Will You place in it one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. After that statement had been made, they made amends in the end by saying: ﴿So forgive those who have repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾. This is like an indication that whoever harms another should preferably compensate for that harm by bringing a benefit to him.

* * *

Know that when the Exalted described the angels as asking forgiveness for those who repent, He explained the manner of that seeking of forgiveness. He related of them that they said: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾. On this there are several issues:

**The first issue:** Supplication in most matters is mentioned with the words "Our Lord" (*rabbana*). The evidence for this is that the angels, when supplicating, said "Our Lord" (*rabbana*), as in this verse. Adam, peace be upon him, said: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves﴾. Noah, peace be upon him, said: ﴿My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge﴾ [Hud: 47]. He also said: ﴿My Lord, I have called to my people night and day﴾ [Nuh: 5], and said: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾ [Nuh: 28]. Of Abraham, peace be upon him, He said: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead﴾ [al-Baqarah: 260], and he said: ﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the day the reckoning takes place﴾ [Ibrahim: 41]. He said: ﴿Our Lord, make us Muslims [submitting] to You, and from our descendants a Muslim nation [submitting] to You﴾ [al-Baqarah: 128]. Of Joseph, He said: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of sovereignty﴾ [Yusuf: 101]. Of Moses, peace be upon him, He said: ﴿My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]. In the account of the striking, He said: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me.' So He forgave him; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.' He said: 'My Lord, for that by which You have favored me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals﴾ [al-Qasas: 17]. The Exalted related of Dawud: ﴿So he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing and turned in repentance﴾ [Sad: 24]. Of Sulayman, He related that he said: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom﴾ [Sad: 35]. Of Zakariyya, that he ﴿called to his Lord in a private call﴾ [Maryam: 3]. Of Isa, peace be upon him, that he said: ﴿Our Lord, send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 114]. Of Muhammad (ﷺ), that Allah the Exalted said to him: ﴿And say: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 97]. He related of the believers that they said: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain﴾ [Al 'Imran: 191], and they repeated this expression five times. He also related of them that they said: ﴿Our Lord, [we seek] Your forgiveness, and to You is the destination﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], up to the end of the surah.

It is established from what we have mentioned that among the most pleasing forms of supplication is that the servant call upon his Lord by saying: "O my Lord." The full difficulty in this is to be stated thus: the word "Allah" is greater than the word "Lord" (*al-Rabb*), so why has the word "Lord" become specific to the time of supplication? The answer: It is as if the servant is saying: "I was in the concealment of non-existence, the pure void and absolute negation, and You brought me out into existence and nurtured me. So make Your nurturing of me an intercessor before You, that You not leave me for the blink of an eye without Your nurturing, Your kindness and Your bounty."

[Page 32]

**The second issue:** The sunnah in supplication is that one begins it with praise of Allah the Exalted, and then mentions the supplication immediately after it. The evidence for this is this verse, for when the angels resolved to supplicate and ask forgiveness for the believers, they began with praise, saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾. Also, when Abraham, peace be upon him, wished to mention the supplication, he first mentioned the praise, saying: ﴿He who created me, and it is He who guides me. And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink. And when I am ill, it is He who cures me. And who will cause me to die and then bring me to life. And who I aspire will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 78–82]. All of this is praise of Allah the Exalted, and after it he mentioned the supplication, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me judgement and join me with the righteous﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 83].

* * *

Know that reason also indicates the observance of this order. The remembrance of Allah through praise and glorification, in relation to the essence of the spirit, is like the supreme elixir in relation to copper. Just as a particle of the elixir, when it falls upon a world of copper, turns the whole into pure gold, so too when a particle of the elixir of knowing the majesty of Allah the Exalted falls upon the essence of the rational spirit, it is transformed from the impurity of copper into the purity of holiness and the permanence of the world of purity. It is thus established that when the light of knowledge of Allah the Exalted shines upon the essences of the spirit, the spirit becomes more pure in clarity and more perfect in illumination. When it becomes so, its power becomes stronger and its influence more perfect, so the attainment of the desired thing through supplication becomes nearer and more complete. This is the reason for placing praise of Allah before supplication.

**The third issue:** Know that the angels described Allah the Exalted with three types of attributes: lordship (*al-rububiyyah*), mercy and knowledge. As for lordship, it indicates bringing into existence and originating. There is another subtle point in it: their saying "Our Lord" (*rabbana*) indicates nurturing (*al-tarbiyah*), and nurturing is an expression for keeping a thing in its most perfect condition and its best attributes. This shows that these contingent beings, just as they are in need at the moment of their coming into being of the bringing into existence and origination by the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, so too they are in need, at the moment of their continuance, of Allah's sustaining them. As for mercy, it indicates that the side of goodness, mercy and kindness outweighs the side of harm, and that He, the Exalted, created creation only for mercy and goodness, not for harm and evil.

If it is said: In the saying ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ there is a problem, because knowledge has encompassed all things, but mercy has not reached all things, since one who is harmed, at the moment he falls into harm, that harm is not mercy. This question is also mentioned in His saying: ﴿My mercy has encompassed all things﴾ [al-A'raf: 156]. We say: Every existent has received a share of the mercy of Allah the Exalted. That is because the existent is either necessary (*wajib*) or contingent (*mumkin*). As for the necessary, there is none but Allah, glorified and exalted is He. As for the contingent, its existence is from Allah the Exalted and by His bringing it into being, and that is mercy. Thus it is established that there is no existent other than Allah except that a portion and an allotment of the mercy of Allah has reached it. Therefore He said: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾.

In the verse there is another subtle point: the angels placed the mention of mercy before the mention of knowledge, saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾. That is because what they sought was the conveying of mercy and that He pass over what He knew of them of kinds of sins. So the thing sought in itself is mercy, and the thing sought incidentally is that He pass over what He knew of them. What is sought in itself takes precedence over what is sought incidentally.

[Page 33]

Do you not see that, since preserving health is sought in itself and removing sickness is sought incidentally, therefore when they defined medicine (*al-tibb*), they placed in it the preservation of health before the removal of sickness, saying: "Medicine is a science by which the conditions of the human body are known, in terms of what becomes sound and what departs from health, so that health may be preserved when present and restored when lost." Likewise here, the thing sought in itself is mercy, while passing over what He knew of them of kinds of sins is sought incidentally, because the attainment of mercy in its complete form is only achieved through passing over sins. For this reason, the mention of mercy came before the mention of knowledge.

**The fourth issue:** This verse indicates that the principal purpose of the first creation and the bringing into being is mercy, bounty, generosity and nobility. The certain proofs indicate that whatever enters existence of kinds of good and evil, happiness and wretchedness, is by the decree and predestination of Allah. Combining these two principles is extremely difficult. At this point the philosophers said: Good is willed and approved, and evil is willed and disliked. Good is decreed by Him in itself, and evil is decreed by Him incidentally. In this there is a great depth.

**The fifth issue:** His saying ﴿You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ indicates that He, glorified is He, knows all the knowables that have no end, both universals and particulars. Furthermore, if this were not so, there would be no benefit in supplication and entreaty, because if it were permissible for some things to fall outside His knowledge, then, under that assumption, the one supplicating would not know that Allah, glorified is He, knows him and knows his supplication, and under that assumption there would remain no benefit whatsoever in supplication.

Know that when the Exalted related of them the manner of their praise of Allah the Exalted, He related of them the manner of their supplication, which is that they said: ﴿So forgive those who have repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾. Know that the angels requested from Allah the Exalted by way of supplication many things for the believers. The first thing requested is forgiveness, and its explanation has already preceded in His saying: ﴿So forgive those who have repented and followed Your way﴾. If it is said: Forgiveness has no meaning except the removal of punishment, and on this assumption there is no difference between His saying "So forgive them" and His saying ﴿and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾. We say: The indication of the word forgiveness on the removal of the punishment of Hellfire is an indication by way of allusion and suggestion. So when they mentioned this supplication by way of allusion and suggestion, they followed it with its mention by way of explicit statement, for the sake of emphasis and intensification. Know that when they asked Allah to remove punishment from them, they followed it by asking Allah to convey reward to them, saying: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eternity which You have promised them﴾. If it is said: You claim that this intercession occurs only for sinners, and this verse refutes that, because the Exalted did not promise sinners that He would admit them into the Gardens of Eternity. We say: We do not concede that He did not promise them that, because we have shown that the many proofs in the Qur'an indicate that He, the Exalted, does not make eternal in the Fire the people of "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." And when He brings them out of the Fire, it is necessary that He admit them into Paradise. Thus this constitutes a promise from Allah the Exalted to them that He will admit them into the Gardens of Eternity, either without entering the Fire or after He has made them enter the Fire.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants﴾. That is: "And admit along with them into Paradise these three groups, namely the righteous among the fathers, the spouses and the descendants." This is because when a man has with him in the setting of his life and his joy his family and his kin, his delight is more complete. Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: "Whoever was righteous" (*man salaha*) is in the accusative case from two positions: if you wish, you may refer it back to the pronoun in His saying ﴿and admit them﴾, and if you wish, to the pronoun in ﴿which You have promised them﴾. The meaning of His saying ﴿whoever was righteous﴾ is the people of faith.

Then they said: ﴿Indeed, You, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾. They mentioned these two attributes in their supplication because, if He were not Mighty, but were such that He could be overpowered and prevented, the requested thing could not occur from Him, and if He were not Wise, this requested thing would not be achieved in accordance with wisdom and benefit.

[Page 34]

Then after that they said: ﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾. Some of them said: The meaning is "protect them from the punishment of evil deeds." If it is said: On this assumption there is no difference between His saying ﴿and protect them from evil deeds﴾ and what preceded of His saying ﴿and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾, and then repetition devoid of benefit would be required, which is impermissible. We say: Rather, the difference arises in two respects. The first: His saying ﴿and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾ is a supplication mentioned for the roots (*usul*), and His saying ﴿and protect them from evil deeds﴾ is a supplication mentioned for the branches (*furu'*). The second: His saying ﴿and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾ is restricted to the removal of Hellfire, while His saying ﴿and protect them from evil deeds﴾ encompasses the punishment of Hellfire, the punishment of the standing place of the Resurrection, and the punishment of the reckoning and questioning.

The second opinion regarding His saying, ﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾, is that the angels asked for the removal of the punishment of the Fire by saying, ﴿And protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, and they asked for the bringing of the reward of Paradise to them by saying, ﴿And admit them to gardens of perpetual residence﴾. Then, after that, they asked that Allah, exalted is He, safeguard them in this world from corrupt beliefs and corrupt deeds, and this is what is meant by their saying, ﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾. Then they said, ﴿And whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day, You have certainly had mercy on him﴾, meaning: whoever You protect from evil deeds in this world, You have certainly had mercy on him on the Day of Resurrection. Then they said, ﴿That is the great success﴾, since they found, through temporary deeds, a bliss that never ends, and through humble deeds, a dominion whose true greatness the intellects cannot reach.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 40, verse 7–9 (part 1 of 3):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise, and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire."﴾ ﴿"Our Lord, and admit them into the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise."﴾ ﴿"And protect them from evil deeds. Whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have indeed shown them mercy. That is the great triumph."﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, explained that the disbelievers exaggerate in displaying enmity towards the believers, He explained that the noblest of the classes of created beings are the angels who are the bearers of the Throne, and those who surround the Throne, who exaggerate in displaying love and support for the believers. It is as if He, exalted is He, says: If these lowly ones exaggerate in enmity, then do not care for them, do not turn to them, and do not give them any weight, for the bearers of the Throne are with you, and those around the Throne are with you, supporting you. There are several issues concerning the verse:

The first issue: He, exalted is He, related this account concerning two kinds of groups of angels:

The first category: ﴿those who bear the Throne﴾. Exalted is He has related that those who bear the Throne on the Day of Resurrection are eight. It may be said: those who bear it at this time are those same eight who will bear it on the Day of Resurrection. And there is no doubt that the bearers of the Throne are the noblest and greatest of the angels. Ṣāḥib al-Kashshāf (al-Zamakhshari) related that the feet of the bearers of the Throne are in the lowest earth and their heads have pierced the Throne, and they are in humble submission, not raising their gaze. And from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not reflect upon the greatness of your Lord, but reflect upon what Allah, exalted is He, has created of the angels, for indeed there is a created angel called Israfil, whose corner of the Throne is upon his shoulder, and his feet are in the lowest earth, and his head has passed through seven heavens, and he shrinks from the greatness of Allah until he becomes like a small thing." It was said: he is a small bird. It has also been narrated that Allah commanded all the angels to greet the bearers of the Throne with peace morning and evening, as a preference for them over the rest of the angels. It was also said: Allah created the Throne from a green jewel, and between two of its legs the flapping of a swiftly flying bird lasts eighty thousand years. It was also said: around the Throne are seventy thousand rows of angels circling it, glorifying and magnifying, and behind them are seventy thousand rows standing with their hands placed upon their shoulders, raising their voices in tahlil and takbir, and behind them are a hundred thousand rows with their right hands placed upon their left. There is not one of them but glorifies with something other than what the other glorifies. I have transmitted these reports from al-Kashshaf.

As for the second category of angels mentioned by Allah in this verse, it is His saying: ﴿and those around it﴾. The more apparent meaning is that what is meant by them is what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord with praise.﴾

I say: Reason indicates that the bearers of the Throne and those surrounding the Throne must be the best of the angels. That is because the relation of spirits to spirits is like the relation of bodies to bodies. So when the Throne was the noblest of corporeal existents, the spirits attached to governing the Throne must be better than the spirits governing bodies. Also, it is likely that there are spirits bearing the body of the Throne, and from those dominant, elevated spirits bearing the body of the Throne there come forth other spirits of their kind, attached to the edges of the Throne, and to them refers His saying: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne.﴾ In sum, it has become clear by certain proofs and by true unveilings that there is no comparison between the world of bodies and the world of spirits. So whatever you witness with the eye of sight in the varying ranks of the world of bodies, you must witness with the eye of insight in the varying ranks of the world of spirits.

The second issue: This verse indicates that He, glorified is He, is far above being in the Throne. That is because He, exalted is He, said in this verse: ﴿those who bear the Throne﴾, and He said in another verse: ﴿And above them on that Day eight will bear the Throne of your Lord﴾ [al-Haqqah: 17]. There is no doubt that the bearer of the Throne is a bearer of everything in the Throne. So if the God of the world were in the Throne, these angels would be bearing the God of the world, and then they would be guarding the God of the world. The guardian, being capable, is more deserving of divinity, and the one borne and guarded is more deserving of servitude. Then the god would become a servant and the servant a god, and that is corrupt. This shows that the God of the Throne and of bodies is exalted above the Throne and bodies.

* * *

Know that He, exalted is He, related three things concerning the bearers of the Throne and those surrounding the Throne:

The first type is His saying: ﴿they glorify their Lord with praise﴾. Its parallel is His saying, relating about the angels: ﴿while we glorify You with Your praise﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30], and His saying: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord with praise.﴾ Thus tasbih is an expression for declaring Allah far above what is unfitting, and tahmid is acknowledging that He is the absolute Bestower of blessings. So tasbih points to majesty (jalal) and tahmid points to generosity (ikram). Thus His saying ﴿they glorify their Lord with praise﴾ is close to His saying: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾ [al-Rahman: 78].

The second type of what Allah related about these angels is His saying: ﴿and they believe in Him.﴾ If it is asked: what is the benefit of His saying ﴿and they believe in Him﴾, since occupation with glorification and praise is not possible unless faith in Allah has already preceded? We say: the benefit in it is what Ṣāḥib al-Kashshāf mentioned, and he did very well in it. He said: the purpose of it is to alert that if Allah were present in the Throne, the bearers of the Throne and those surrounding the Throne would be seeing Him and witnessing Him. And since their belief in the existence of Allah entails praise and commendation, because affirming the existence of a present, seen, witnessed thing does not entail praise and commendation (do you not see that affirming the existence of the sun and that it is luminous does not entail praise and commendation?), when Allah mentioned their belief in Him in the manner of praise, commendation and exaltation, it became known that they believed in Him, as evidenced by the fact that they did not see Him present and sitting there. May Allah have mercy on Ṣāḥib al-Kashshāf; had he not included in his book anything but this point, it would have sufficed him as pride and honour.

The third type of what Allah related about these angels is His saying: ﴿and they ask forgiveness for those who believe.﴾ Know that it is established that complete happiness is tied to two matters: exalting the command of Allah, and compassion toward the creation of Allah. And it is necessary that exalting the command of Allah be prior to compassion toward the creation of Allah. So His saying ﴿they glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him﴾ indicates exalting the command of Allah, and His saying
صفحة ٣٠
﴿and they ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾ indicates compassion toward the creation of Allah.

Then there are several issues in the verse:

The first issue: Many scholars have used this verse to establish that the angel is better than the human. They said: this verse indicates that when the angels finished mentioning Allah with praise and sanctification, they occupied themselves with seeking forgiveness for others, namely the believers. This shows that they are independent of seeking forgiveness for themselves; for if they were in need of it, they would have put seeking forgiveness for themselves before seeking forgiveness for others, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Begin with yourself." Also Allah said to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So know that there is no god but Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women﴾ [Muhammad: 19]; so He commanded Muhammad to mention first seeking forgiveness for himself, and after that to seek forgiveness for others. And He related of Nuh, peace be upon him, that he said: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house believing, and the believing men and believing women﴾ [Nuh: 28]. This indicates that everyone who is in need of forgiveness puts seeking forgiveness for himself before seeking it for others. So if the angels were in need of forgiveness, their occupation with seeking forgiveness for themselves would have preceded their occupation with seeking it for others. And since Allah did not mention from them their seeking forgiveness for themselves, we know that this was because they were not in need of forgiveness. As for the prophets, peace be upon them, they were in need of forgiveness, based on His saying to Muhammad, peace be upon him: ﴿and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. And if this is established, then it is clear that the angel is better than the human. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: al-Ka'bi used this verse to establish that the effect of intercession is in the increase of reward for believers, not in removing punishment from sinners. He said: that is because the angels said: ﴿So forgive those who repent and follow Your way﴾. He said: what is meant is not "forgive those who repented from disbelief," whether he was persisting in sin or not, because one whose state is such is not described as following the way of his Lord, and that is not applied to him. Also the angels say: ﴿and admit them into the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them﴾, and this is not fitting for the wicked, because our opponents do not affirm with certainty that Allah promised them Paradise; they only permit that. So it is established that the intercession of the angels only reaches the people of obedience, and so the intercession of the prophets must be the same, since there is no one who makes a distinction. The answer: we say this verse indicates the occurrence of intercession from the angels for sinners. We will explain this, then answer what al-Ka'bi mentioned. As for the explanation of how this verse indicates what we have said, it is from several aspects:

The first: His saying: ﴿and they ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾. Seeking forgiveness is requesting forgiveness, and forgiveness is only mentioned in the removal of punishment. As for requesting an additional benefit, it is not called seeking forgiveness.

The second: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾, and this indicates that they seek forgiveness for every people of faith. So when we establish that the person who commits a major sin is a believer, it is necessary that he enter under this intercession.

The third: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So forgive those who repent﴾. Requesting forgiveness for those who repent: it is not permissible that what is meant is the removal of punishment for a major sin after repentance, because that is obligatory upon Allah according to the opponent, and what is obligatory in action, asking for it by supplication is ugly. Nor is it permissible that what is meant is the removal of punishment for minor sins, because that too is obligatory, so asking for it by supplication is not fitting. Nor is it permissible that what is meant is requesting an increase in benefit beyond the reward, because that is not called forgiveness. So it is established that His saying ﴿So forgive those who repent﴾ cannot be understood except as the removal of the punishment for a major sin before repentance. And if this is established regarding the angels, then likewise regarding the prophets, since consensus is established that there is no difference. As for what al-Ka'bi relies on, namely that they requested forgiveness for those who repented, we say: it must be that what is meant by it is those who repented from disbelief and followed the way of faith. As for his saying that one who repents from disbelief while persisting in wickedness is not called a penitent nor one who follows the way of Allah, we say: we do not concede his statement; rather it is said: he is a penitent from disbelief and a follower of the way of Allah in religion and law. And when it is established that he is a penitent from disbelief, it is established that he is a penitent. Do you not see that for the truth of describing someone as a striker or a laugher, it suffices that striking or laughing proceeds from him once, and that does not depend on all kinds of striking or laughing proceeding from him? So likewise here.

**Third issue:** The people of verification (*ahl al-tahqiq*) said: This intercession by the angels on behalf of humankind takes the form of an apology for a past lapse. When the angels first learned of the creation of humans, they said: ﴿Will You place in it one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. After that statement had been made, they made amends in the end by saying: ﴿So forgive those who have repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾. This is like an indication that whoever harms another should preferably compensate for that harm by bringing a benefit to him.

* * *

Know that when the Exalted described the angels as asking forgiveness for those who repent, He explained the manner of that seeking of forgiveness. He related of them that they said: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾. On this there are several issues:

**The first issue:** Supplication in most matters is mentioned with the words "Our Lord" (*rabbana*). The evidence for this is that the angels, when supplicating, said "Our Lord" (*rabbana*), as in this verse. Adam, peace be upon him, said: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves﴾. Noah, peace be upon him, said: ﴿My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge﴾ [Hud: 47]. He also said: ﴿My Lord, I have called to my people night and day﴾ [Nuh: 5], and said: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾ [Nuh: 28]. Of Abraham, peace be upon him, He said: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead﴾ [al-Baqarah: 260], and he said: ﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the day the reckoning takes place﴾ [Ibrahim: 41]. He said: ﴿Our Lord, make us Muslims [submitting] to You, and from our descendants a Muslim nation [submitting] to You﴾ [al-Baqarah: 128]. Of Joseph, He said: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of sovereignty﴾ [Yusuf: 101]. Of Moses, peace be upon him, He said: ﴿My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]. In the account of the striking, He said: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me.' So He forgave him; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.' He said: 'My Lord, for that by which You have favored me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals﴾ [al-Qasas: 17]. The Exalted related of Dawud: ﴿So he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing and turned in repentance﴾ [Sad: 24]. Of Sulayman, He related that he said: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom﴾ [Sad: 35]. Of Zakariyya, that he ﴿called to his Lord in a private call﴾ [Maryam: 3]. Of Isa, peace be upon him, that he said: ﴿Our Lord, send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 114]. Of Muhammad (ﷺ), that Allah the Exalted said to him: ﴿And say: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 97]. He related of the believers that they said: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain﴾ [Al 'Imran: 191], and they repeated this expression five times. He also related of them that they said: ﴿Our Lord, [we seek] Your forgiveness, and to You is the destination﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], up to the end of the surah.

It is established from what we have mentioned that among the most pleasing forms of supplication is that the servant call upon his Lord by saying: "O my Lord." The full difficulty in this is to be stated thus: the word "Allah" is greater than the word "Lord" (*al-Rabb*), so why has the word "Lord" become specific to the time of supplication? The answer: It is as if the servant is saying: "I was in the concealment of non-existence, the pure void and absolute negation, and You brought me out into existence and nurtured me. So make Your nurturing of me an intercessor before You, that You not leave me for the blink of an eye without Your nurturing, Your kindness and Your bounty."

[Page 32]

**The second issue:** The sunnah in supplication is that one begins it with praise of Allah the Exalted, and then mentions the supplication immediately after it. The evidence for this is this verse, for when the angels resolved to supplicate and ask forgiveness for the believers, they began with praise, saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾. Also, when Abraham, peace be upon him, wished to mention the supplication, he first mentioned the praise, saying: ﴿He who created me, and it is He who guides me. And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink. And when I am ill, it is He who cures me. And who will cause me to die and then bring me to life. And who I aspire will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 78–82]. All of this is praise of Allah the Exalted, and after it he mentioned the supplication, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me judgement and join me with the righteous﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 83].

* * *

Know that reason also indicates the observance of this order. The remembrance of Allah through praise and glorification, in relation to the essence of the spirit, is like the supreme elixir in relation to copper. Just as a particle of the elixir, when it falls upon a world of copper, turns the whole into pure gold, so too when a particle of the elixir of knowing the majesty of Allah the Exalted falls upon the essence of the rational spirit, it is transformed from the impurity of copper into the purity of holiness and the permanence of the world of purity. It is thus established that when the light of knowledge of Allah the Exalted shines upon the essences of the spirit, the spirit becomes more pure in clarity and more perfect in illumination. When it becomes so, its power becomes stronger and its influence more perfect, so the attainment of the desired thing through supplication becomes nearer and more complete. This is the reason for placing praise of Allah before supplication.

**The third issue:** Know that the angels described Allah the Exalted with three types of attributes: lordship (*al-rububiyyah*), mercy and knowledge. As for lordship, it indicates bringing into existence and originating. There is another subtle point in it: their saying "Our Lord" (*rabbana*) indicates nurturing (*al-tarbiyah*), and nurturing is an expression for keeping a thing in its most perfect condition and its best attributes. This shows that these contingent beings, just as they are in need at the moment of their coming into being of the bringing into existence and origination by the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, so too they are in need, at the moment of their continuance, of Allah's sustaining them. As for mercy, it indicates that the side of goodness, mercy and kindness outweighs the side of harm, and that He, the Exalted, created creation only for mercy and goodness, not for harm and evil.

If it is said: In the saying ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ there is a problem, because knowledge has encompassed all things, but mercy has not reached all things, since one who is harmed, at the moment he falls into harm, that harm is not mercy. This question is also mentioned in His saying: ﴿My mercy has encompassed all things﴾ [al-A'raf: 156]. We say: Every existent has received a share of the mercy of Allah the Exalted. That is because the existent is either necessary (*wajib*) or contingent (*mumkin*). As for the necessary, there is none but Allah, glorified and exalted is He. As for the contingent, its existence is from Allah the Exalted and by His bringing it into being, and that is mercy. Thus it is established that there is no existent other than Allah except that a portion and an allotment of the mercy of Allah has reached it. Therefore He said: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾.

In the verse there is another subtle point: the angels placed the mention of mercy before the mention of knowledge, saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾. That is because what they sought was the conveying of mercy and that He pass over what He knew of them of kinds of sins. So the thing sought in itself is mercy, and the thing sought incidentally is that He pass over what He knew of them. What is sought in itself takes precedence over what is sought incidentally.

[Page 33]

Do you not see that, since preserving health is sought in itself and removing sickness is sought incidentally, therefore when they defined medicine (*al-tibb*), they placed in it the preservation of health before the removal of sickness, saying: "Medicine is a science by which the conditions of the human body are known, in terms of what becomes sound and what departs from health, so that health may be preserved when present and restored when lost." Likewise here, the thing sought in itself is mercy, while passing over what He knew of them of kinds of sins is sought incidentally, because the attainment of mercy in its complete form is only achieved through passing over sins. For this reason, the mention of mercy came before the mention of knowledge.

**The fourth issue:** This verse indicates that the principal purpose of the first creation and the bringing into being is mercy, bounty, generosity and nobility. The certain proofs indicate that whatever enters existence of kinds of good and evil, happiness and wretchedness, is by the decree and predestination of Allah. Combining these two principles is extremely difficult. At this point the philosophers said: Good is willed and approved, and evil is willed and disliked. Good is decreed by Him in itself, and evil is decreed by Him incidentally. In this there is a great depth.

**The fifth issue:** His saying ﴿You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ indicates that He, glorified is He, knows all the knowables that have no end, both universals and particulars. Furthermore, if this were not so, there would be no benefit in supplication and entreaty, because if it were permissible for some things to fall outside His knowledge, then, under that assumption, the one supplicating would not know that Allah, glorified is He, knows him and knows his supplication, and under that assumption there would remain no benefit whatsoever in supplication.

Know that when the Exalted related of them the manner of their praise of Allah the Exalted, He related of them the manner of their supplication, which is that they said: ﴿So forgive those who have repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾. Know that the angels requested from Allah the Exalted by way of supplication many things for the believers. The first thing requested is forgiveness, and its explanation has already preceded in His saying: ﴿So forgive those who have repented and followed Your way﴾. If it is said: Forgiveness has no meaning except the removal of punishment, and on this assumption there is no difference between His saying "So forgive them" and His saying ﴿and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾. We say: The indication of the word forgiveness on the removal of the punishment of Hellfire is an indication by way of allusion and suggestion. So when they mentioned this supplication by way of allusion and suggestion, they followed it with its mention by way of explicit statement, for the sake of emphasis and intensification. Know that when they asked Allah to remove punishment from them, they followed it by asking Allah to convey reward to them, saying: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eternity which You have promised them﴾. If it is said: You claim that this intercession occurs only for sinners, and this verse refutes that, because the Exalted did not promise sinners that He would admit them into the Gardens of Eternity. We say: We do not concede that He did not promise them that, because we have shown that the many proofs in the Qur'an indicate that He, the Exalted, does not make eternal in the Fire the people of "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." And when He brings them out of the Fire, it is necessary that He admit them into Paradise. Thus this constitutes a promise from Allah the Exalted to them that He will admit them into the Gardens of Eternity, either without entering the Fire or after He has made them enter the Fire.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants﴾. That is: "And admit along with them into Paradise these three groups, namely the righteous among the fathers, the spouses and the descendants." This is because when a man has with him in the setting of his life and his joy his family and his kin, his delight is more complete. Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: "Whoever was righteous" (*man salaha*) is in the accusative case from two positions: if you wish, you may refer it back to the pronoun in His saying ﴿and admit them﴾, and if you wish, to the pronoun in ﴿which You have promised them﴾. The meaning of His saying ﴿whoever was righteous﴾ is the people of faith.

Then they said: ﴿Indeed, You, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾. They mentioned these two attributes in their supplication because, if He were not Mighty, but were such that He could be overpowered and prevented, the requested thing could not occur from Him, and if He were not Wise, this requested thing would not be achieved in accordance with wisdom and benefit.

[Page 34]

Then after that they said: ﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾. Some of them said: The meaning is "protect them from the punishment of evil deeds." If it is said: On this assumption there is no difference between His saying ﴿and protect them from evil deeds﴾ and what preceded of His saying ﴿and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾, and then repetition devoid of benefit would be required, which is impermissible. We say: Rather, the difference arises in two respects. The first: His saying ﴿and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾ is a supplication mentioned for the roots (*usul*), and His saying ﴿and protect them from evil deeds﴾ is a supplication mentioned for the branches (*furu'*). The second: His saying ﴿and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾ is restricted to the removal of Hellfire, while His saying ﴿and protect them from evil deeds﴾ encompasses the punishment of Hellfire, the punishment of the standing place of the Resurrection, and the punishment of the reckoning and questioning.

The second opinion regarding His saying, ﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾, is that the angels asked for the removal of the punishment of the Fire by saying, ﴿And protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, and they asked for the bringing of the reward of Paradise to them by saying, ﴿And admit them to gardens of perpetual residence﴾. Then, after that, they asked that Allah, exalted is He, safeguard them in this world from corrupt beliefs and corrupt deeds, and this is what is meant by their saying, ﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾. Then they said, ﴿And whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day, You have certainly had mercy on him﴾, meaning: whoever You protect from evil deeds in this world, You have certainly had mercy on him on the Day of Resurrection. Then they said, ﴿That is the great success﴾, since they found, through temporary deeds, a bliss that never ends, and through humble deeds, a dominion whose true greatness the intellects cannot reach.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 40, verses 10–12 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to: The hatred of Allah is greater than your hatred of yourselves, when you were called to the faith but you disbelieved.﴾ ﴿They will say: Our Lord, You have made us die twice and given us life twice, so we have acknowledged our sins. Is there any way out?﴾ ﴿That is because, when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.﴾

Know that when He, may He be exalted, returned to explaining the state of the disbelieving disputers in the signs of Allah, who are those Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve﴾ [Ghafir: 4], He made clear that on the Day of Resurrection they will acknowledge their sins and their deserving of the punishment that will descend upon them, and they will ask to be returned to the world so that they may make up for what they neglected. So He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to: The hatred of Allah is greater than your hatred [of yourselves]﴾. In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: In the verse there is an omission (hadhf) and also an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir). As for the omission, its estimated form is "the hatred of Allah toward you" (lamaqtu Allahi iyyakum). As for the inversion, the sense is to say: "The hatred of Allah toward you at the time you were called to the faith but you disbelieved is greater than your hatred of yourselves." Regarding the interpretation of their hatred of themselves, there are several views:

The first: When they witness the Resurrection, Paradise and Hell, they will hate themselves for their persistence in denying these things in the world.

The second: The followers will intensely hate the leaders who called them to disbelief in the world, and the leaders will also intensely hate the followers. So he expressed the hatred of some of them toward others as their hating themselves, just as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So kill yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 54], while the intended meaning is that some of them kill others.

The third: Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: When Iblis addresses them while they are in the Fire with His saying: ﴿I had no authority over you ... ﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and blame yourselves﴾ [Ibrahim: 22], then at that moment they hate themselves.

Know that there is no dispute that their hatred of themselves occurs only on the Day of Resurrection. As for Allah's hatred toward them, there are two views:

The first: It exists in the Hereafter, and the meaning is: Allah's hatred toward you at this time is greater than your hatred of yourselves at this time.

The second, which is the view of most, is that the estimated meaning is: Allah's hatred toward you in the world, when you were called to the faith but you disbelieved, is greater than your hatred of yourselves now.

Regarding the interpretation of the words mentioned in the verse, there are several views. The first: those who call out to them and speak these words to them are the guardians of Hell (khazanat Jahannam). The second: hatred (maqt) is the most intense dislike, and that in relation to Allah, may He be exalted, is impossible, so what is meant by it is the most emphatic denunciation and rebuke. The third: al-Farra' said: "They are called out to: Indeed the hatred of Allah toward you when you were called to the faith but you came with disbelief is greater than your hatred of yourselves now."

Then He, may He be exalted, made clear that when the disbelievers are addressed with this address: ﴿They will say: Our Lord, You have made us die twice...﴾ to the end of the verse. The meaning is that when they realized that what they were upon in the world was corrupt and false, they wished to return to the world so that upon returning they would busy themselves with righteous deeds. In the verse there are issues:

The first issue: Most scholars have used this verse to establish the punishment of the grave. The argument is that they affirmed for themselves two deaths when they said: ﴿Our Lord, You have made us die twice﴾. One of the two deaths is witnessed in the world, so there must be an affirmation of another life in the grave, so that the death that occurs after it becomes a second death. This indicates that there is life in the grave. If it is said: Many exegetes said that the first death refers to the state when a human is a drop (nutfah) and a clinging clot ('alaqah), and the second death refers to what occurs in the world, so why could the matter not be like that? What shows that the matter is as we have mentioned is His saying: ﴿How do you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life, then He will cause you to die﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28]. The meaning of "you were dead" is the state when he was a drop and a clot. The precise statement is that causing death (al-imatah) is used in two senses: one is bringing a thing into existence dead; the second is making a thing dead after it was alive, as when you say: "The tailor widened my garment," which may mean that he sewed it wide, or that he made it wide after it was narrow. So why could it not be in this verse that the meaning of causing death is creating them dead, and not making them dead after they were alive?

The second question: This is the speech of the disbelievers, so it is not evidence.

The third question: This verse indicates the denial of the occurrence of life in the grave. As for rational evidence, it is in several ways:

The first: The one who was seized by predators and eaten, if he were restored alive, would either be restored alive as a whole or in individual parts. The first is false, since sense perception shows that no whole was produced for him. The second is false, because when predators ate him, if those parts were made alive, they would be alive in the stomachs and intestines of the predators, and that is extremely far-fetched.

The second: If we left the dead one exposed so that everyone could see him, they would see him still in his death. The second: Perhaps they mentioned the two lives, namely life in the world and life in the Resurrection, and neglected to mention life in the grave because of its scarcity and the brevity of its duration.
