This is the meaning of acquisition, and the meaning of that acquisition necessitating recompense. Thus it becomes clear that the full recompense is attained only on the Day of Resurrection. This is a universal rational principle, and the true Law has come with what strengthens this universal principle in the details of deeds and words. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: this verse is a great foundation in the principles of jurisprudence (*usul al-fiqh*). We say: if any kind of harm were lawfully prescribed, it would either be prescribed as a recompense for some offense or not as a recompense. Both alternatives are invalid, so the claim that it is prescribed is invalid. As for the proof that it cannot be prescribed as a recompense for some deed: this text requires the postponement of recompenses until the Day of Resurrection, so establishing it in this world would contradict this text. As for the proof that it cannot be prescribed as a recompense, [it follows] from His saying: ﴿Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], and His saying: ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ [al-Hajj: 78], and His, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: "There is no harm and no reciprocating harm in Islam." We have departed from these general statements in cases where the harms are recompenses, and in cases where a text has permitted them, such as the slaughter of animals. So it is necessary that the rest remain on the original prohibition. From what we have mentioned it is established that the basic rule concerning harms and pains is prohibition. If we find a specific text indicating legitimacy, we judge by it, giving precedence to the specific over the general. Otherwise it remains on the original prohibition. This is a universal principle, of much benefit in the Law. And Allah knows best.

The sixth attribute of that Day is His saying: ﴿There is no injustice today﴾. The purpose is that when He said: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned﴾, He followed it with something indicating that no kind of injustice occurs on that Day. The verifiers (*al-muhaqqiqun*) said: injustice in recompense occurs in four ways. The first: a person deserves a reward but is denied it. The second: one party gives another part of what is due to him but does not deliver his full right. The third: one punishes someone who does not deserve punishment. The fourth: a person deserves punishment and is punished, but is punished beyond the measure of what he deserves. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿There is no injustice today﴾ indicates the negation of these four kinds. The judge (*al-Qadi*) said: this verse is strong in refuting the view of the Jabriyya (determinists), because according to their doctrine, there is no injustice at all, either apparent or real, except from Allah. Moreover, if He creates disbelief in a person and then punishes him for it, this is the very essence of injustice. The answer to this is well known.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. The mention of this statement in this place is very fitting, because when He made clear that there is no injustice, He made clear that He is swift in reckoning. This indicates that what they deserve will reach them immediately. And Allah knows best.

[Page 38]

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs and sends down provision for you from the sky. Yet none remembers except one who turns back (to God).﴾ ﴿So call upon God, making your religion sincerely His, though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned what necessitates severe threat against the polytheists, He followed it with mention of what indicates the perfection of His power and wisdom, so that this would serve as proof that it is not permissible to make these carved stones and shaped wood partners with God, exalted is He, in worship. So He said: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs.﴾ Know that the most important of important matters is the safeguarding of the interests of religions and the interests of bodies. He, glorified and exalted is He, safeguarded the interests of the religions of His servants by manifesting the clear proofs and signs, and He safeguarded the interests of their bodies by sending down provision from the sky. Thus the place of signs with regard to religions is like the place of provisions with regard to bodies. Signs are for the life of religions, and provisions are for the life of bodies. When both are attained, favour is accomplished in the strongest of considerations and the most complete of aspects.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Yet none remembers except one who turns back (to God).﴾ The meaning is that standing upon the proofs of God's oneness is like a matter fixed in the intellect, except that affirming partnership and occupying oneself with worship of other than God becomes like a barrier against the manifestation of those lights. So when the servant turns away from these and turns back to God, exalted is He, the veil and the covering are removed, and complete success becomes apparent. When He had established this meaning, He stated the desired matter explicitly, which is turning away from other than God and fully turning toward God, exalted is He. So He said: ﴿So call upon God, making your religion sincerely His﴾ — free of polytheism and of inclination toward anything other than God. ﴿Though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ Ibn Kathir read *yunzilu* (﴿يُنَزِّلُ﴾, "He sends down") with a light (single-consonant) form, while the rest read it with the doubled form.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Exalted in degrees, Lord of the Throne, He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, that He may warn of the Day of Meeting, the Day when they will come forth, nothing of them being hidden from God. Whose is the dominion today? It is God's, the One, the Subduer.﴾ ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. There is no injustice today. Indeed God is swift in reckoning.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned among the attributes of His majesty and generosity that He manifests signs and sends down provisions, He mentioned in this verse three other attributes of majesty and greatness, which is His saying: ﴿Exalted in degrees, Lord of the Throne, He casts the Spirit.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf said: "Three predicates of His saying 'He' (huwa) are arranged upon His saying ﴿who shows you﴾, or they are predicates of an omitted subject, and they differ in definiteness and indefiniteness. It has been read *rafī'a al-darajāt* (﴿رَفِيعَ الدَّرَجاتِ﴾) in the accusative as a form of praise."

I say: It is necessary to explain these three attributes.

As for the first attribute, His saying ﴿Exalted in degrees﴾: know that *al-rafī'* may be taken to mean the one who raises, or it may be taken to mean the one who is exalted. If we take it in the first sense, there are several aspects:

The first aspect: He, exalted is He, raises the degrees of the prophets and the friends of God in Paradise.

The second: He raises the degrees of creation in knowledge and in praiseworthy character. He, glorified is He, assigned to each of the angels a specific degree, as He said: ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station﴾ [al-Saffat: 164]. He assigned to each of the scholars a specific degree, as He said: ﴿God will raise those among you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 11]. He assigned to each body a specific degree: some of them are lowly and elemental, some are stellar and astral, and some are from the substances of the Throne and the Footstool. He gave some of them a higher degree than the degree of others. Also, He assigned to each one a specific rank in creation, provision and term of life, as He said: ﴿It is He who made you successors on the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees﴾ [al-An'am: 165]. He assigned to each of the happy and the wretched in this world a specific degree of the causes of happiness and the causes of wretchedness, and in the Hereafter there are effects that manifest that happiness and wretchedness. So if we take *al-rafī'* to mean the one who raises, its meaning is what we have mentioned.

If we take it to mean the one who is exalted, then He, glorified is He, is the most exalted of existents in all attributes of perfection and majesty. As for existence itself, He is the most exalted of existents,

[Page 39]

because He is necessarily existent in Himself (wājib al-wujūd li-dhātihi), while everything other than Him is contingent (mumkin) and in need of Him. As for the permanence of existence, He is the most exalted of existents, because He is necessarily existent in Himself. He is the Eternal, the Everlasting, the Perpetual, who is the first of everything other than Him and has no first, and the last of everything other than Him and has no last. As for knowledge, He is the One who knows all essences, attributes, universals and particulars, as He said: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. As for power, He is the highest of the powerful and the most exalted of them, because in His existence and in all the perfections of His existence He is independent of everything other than Him, while everything other than Him is in need of Him in its existence and in all the perfections of its existence. As for unity, He is the One for whom it is impossible to have an opposite, a peer, a partner or an equal.

I say: The Truth, glorified is He, has two attributes. The first: His independence in His existence and in all the attributes of His existence from everything other than Him. The second: the dependence of everything other than Him upon Him in its existence and in the attributes of its existence. So *al-rafī'*, if we interpret it as "the exalted," its meaning is that He is the most exalted and highest of existents in all attributes of majesty and honour. If we interpret it as "the one who raises," its meaning is that every degree, virtue, mercy and distinction that has come to something other than Him has come only through His bringing it into existence, His originating it, His bounty and His mercy.

The second attribute: His saying ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾. Its meaning is that He is the owner of the Throne, its administrator and its creator. Some ignorant ones among the anthropomorphists (*mushabbihah*) argued with His saying ﴿Exalted in degrees, Lord of the Throne﴾, understanding by "degrees" the heavens, and by "Lord of the Throne" that He is present on the Throne above the seven heavens. They have greatly slandered God, exalted is He. We have shown by compelling rational proofs that His being a body and being in a direction is impossible. Also, the apparent wording does not indicate what they have claimed, because His saying ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾ indicates nothing more than His being related to the Throne, and to be related to it suffices by His being its owner and bringing it from non-existence into existence. So what necessity compels us to go to the false saying and the corrupt doctrine? The benefit of specifying the Throne by mention is that it is the greatest of bodies, and the aim is to show the perfection of His divinity and the penetration of His power. Whenever the locus of disposal and governance is greater, its indication of perfect power is stronger.

* * *

The third attribute: His saying ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants.﴾ Concerning it there are several discussions.

The first discussion: They differed about what is meant by this Spirit. The correct view is that what is meant is revelation (*al-wahy*). We have expanded in explaining why revelation was named "Spirit" at the beginning of Surah al-Nahl, in explaining His saying ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command﴾ [al-Nahl: 2]. He also said: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life?﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. The summary of the matter is that the life of spirits is through divine knowledge and holy manifestations. When revelation is the cause of the attainment of these spirits, it is named "Spirit," just as the spirit is the cause of attaining life, and revelation is the cause of attaining this spiritual life.

Know that this verse contains wondrous secrets from the sciences of unveilings. This is because the perfection of God's greatness cannot be reached by intellects and understandings. So the complete way of describing Him, within the human capacity, is that this statement be mentioned in its general rational form, and then something of perceptible things be mentioned after it, confirming that rational meaning, so that the description through this method supports the intellect. Here too it is like that. So His saying ﴿Exalted in degrees﴾ either means that He is raising degrees, which is an indication of the influence of God's power in bringing into existence contingent things with their differing degrees and varied ranks and attributes, or it means that He, exalted is He, is exalted in attributes of majesty and qualities of might above all existents. This statement is rational and demonstrative. Then He, glorified is He, explained this general statement with further elaboration. This is because what is other than God, exalted is He, is either corporeal things or [Page 40] spiritual things. So in this verse He explained that both kinds are subjected under the subjugation of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. As for corporeal things, the greatest of them is the Throne. So His saying ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾ indicates His dominance over the whole world of bodies. Since the Throne is of the kind of perceptible things, this perceptible thing confirms that intelligible meaning, I mean His saying ﴿Exalted in degrees﴾. As for spiritual things, all of them are subjected to the Truth, glorified is He, and to this the indication is His saying ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command.﴾

Know that the most noble of the apparent states in the spiritual beings of this world is the manifestation of the effects of revelation. Revelation is completed only by four pillars. The first of them is the Sender, who is God, glorified and exalted is He; for this reason He attributed the casting of revelation to Himself, saying ﴿He casts the Spirit.﴾ The second pillar is the sending and the revelation, which He named "the Spirit." The third pillar is that the arrival of revelation from God to the prophets is not possible except through the intermediary of the angels, and this is what is indicated in this verse by His saying ﴿by His command.﴾ So the spiritual pillar is called "command," as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command﴾ [Fussilat: 12], and He said: ﴿Surely to Him belong creation and command﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. The fourth pillar is the prophets to whom God casts revelation, and this is what is indicated by His saying ﴿upon whom He wills of His servants.﴾ The fifth pillar is the specification of the purpose and the original aim of casting this revelation to them. That is, the prophets, peace be upon them, turn people from the world of this life to the world of the Hereafter, and lead them to turn away from these bodily things and turn toward spiritual things. To this the indication is His saying ﴿that He may warn of the Day of Meeting, the Day when they will come forth.﴾ This is a wondrous arrangement that points to these lofty indications from the divine sciences of unveilings.

It remains here for us to clarify: what is the reason for calling the Day of Resurrection "the Day of Meeting," and how many attributes did God mention in this surah for the Day of Meeting?

As for the reason for calling the Day of Resurrection "the Day of Meeting," there are several views:

The first: Spirits were separated from bodies, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, spirits will meet bodies, so that day is the Day of Meeting.

The second: creatures will meet one another in it, so some of them will be informed of the state of others.

The third: the people of heaven will descend to the people of earth, so the people of heaven and the people of earth will meet on it. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And on the Day the heaven will be split open with clouds and the angels will be sent down, descending﴾ [al-Furqan: 25].

The fourth: everyone reaches the recompense of his deed on that day, and so it is from the sense of meeting, taken from the saying of people: "So-and-so met his deed."

The fifth: it may be taken from His saying: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110], and from His saying: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be "Peace"﴾ [al-Ahzab: 44].

The sixth: it is a day on which those who worship and those who are worshipped meet.

The seventh: it is a day on which Adam, peace be upon him, meets his last child.

The eighth: Maymun ibn Mihran said: it is a day on which the oppressor and the oppressed meet. A man may wrong another man and then separate from him; if he wanted to find him he would not be able to, nor recognise him. But on the Day of Resurrection they will both be present, and they will meet one another.

Ibn Kathir read (*al-talāqī wal-tanādī*, ﴿التَّلاقِي وَالتَّنادِي﴾) with the letter *yā'* affirmed both in continuation and at pause, and (*hādī* and *wāqī*, ﴿هادِي وواقِي﴾) with *yā'* at pause and with tanwin in continuation.

As for explaining how many attributes God counted and described the Day of Resurrection with in this verse, we say:

**Part 2 of 2**

The first attribute: the Day of Encounter (*yawm al-talaq*), which we have already explained.

The second attribute is His saying: ﴿the Day when they will come forth (*bariz*n*)﴾. There are several interpretations of this "coming forth":

The first: they will come forth from the depths of their graves.

The second: *bariz*n* means "manifest," that is, nothing will conceal them from a mountain, a hill, or a building, because the earth will be level and bare, a flat plain (*qa' safsaf*). Nor will they wear clothing; rather they will be naked and exposed, as has come in the hadith: "They will be gathered naked, barefoot and uncircumcised (*ghurl*)."

The third: their being manifest may be taken as a metaphor for the exposure of their deeds and the uncovering of their secrets, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿On the Day when the hidden things are tested﴾ [al-Tariq: 9].

The fourth: these rational human souls, in this world, are as if they were immersed in the darkness of the deeds of the bodies. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they turn away from occupation with managing corporeal matters and turn entirely toward the world of the Resurrection and the assembly of spiritual realities. It is as if they come forth after having been hidden within corporeal things and concealed by them.

The third attribute: His saying ﴿nothing of them is hidden from Allah﴾. The meaning is a Day on which nothing of them will be hidden from Allah, and the purpose of this is a warning. He, exalted is He, has made clear that when they come forth from their graves, gather, and meet, Allah, exalted is He, knows what each one of them has done, and He will recompense each according to his deeds: if good, then good; if evil, then evil. Even if they do not know the details of what they did, Allah, exalted is He, knows all of it. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿On that Day you will be presented, and nothing of you will be hidden﴾ [al-Haqqah: 18]. He also said: ﴿On the Day when the hidden things are tested﴾ [al-Tariq: 9], and ﴿When what is in the graves is scattered and what is in the breasts is brought out﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 9–10], and ﴿On that Day she will report her news﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 4].

If it is objected: Allah is not hidden from anything of them on all days, so what is the point of restricting this meaning to that Day? We say: In this world, when they hid behind walls and veils, they imagined that Allah did not see them and that their deeds were hidden from Him. On that Day, they pass into a state of being exposed and laid bare, in which they will not imagine what they imagined in this world. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do﴾ [Fussilat: 22], and He said: ﴿They hide from people, but they do not hide from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 108]. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾.

* * *

The fourth attribute: His exalted saying ﴿Whose is the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾. The implied sense is a Day on which it will be called out: "Whose is the dominion today?" As to when this call occurs, there are two opinions:

The first: the commentators said that when everything in the heavens and the earth has perished, the Lord, exalted is He, will say: ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection. No one will answer Him, so He answers Himself: ﴿To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾. The scholars of usul (*usul al-fiqh*, the principles of jurisprudence) said: this view is weak, and its weakness is shown in several ways:

The first: He, exalted is He, has made clear that this call takes place on the Day of Encounter, the Day of Coming Forth, and the Day when every soul is recompensed for what it earned. At that time, people are alive. So their claim that Allah calls out this call only after everything in the heavens and the earth has perished is refuted.

The second: speech must have a purpose, because speech is either uttered in the presence of another or in the absence of another. The first is invalid here, because those people say that He, exalted is He, mentions this only when all things have perished. The second is also invalid, because a person speaks in solitude either to memorize something, as one repeats a lesson, and that is impossible for Allah; or for the sake of delight in what he says, and that too is impossible for Allah; or in order to worship Allah through that remembrance, and that too is impossible for Allah. Thus it is established that the view of one who says that Allah, exalted is He, mentions this call at the time of the destruction of all creatures is false and has no basis.

The second opinion: on the Day of Encounter, when the first and the last have assembled and come forth before Allah, a caller calls out: ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾, and all who are present in the assembly of the Resurrection answer: ﴿To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾. The believers say it with delight, because by this remembrance they attain an exalted station, while the disbelievers say it in abasement and humiliation, out of regret and remorse that this remembrance escaped them in the world. Those who hold this view said: even if the first opinion is reported from Ibn 'Abbas and others, it is not impossible that the intended meaning is that this call is made after the destruction of humankind, but that there were angels present there who heard that call. I also say on this view: it is not far-fetched that the one asking and the one answering is Allah, exalted is He; nor is it far-fetched that the one asking is a group of angels and the one answering is another group. All of these are possible, and there is no definite proof for any one of them.

If it is asked: what is the benefit of restricting this call to this Day?

We say: people were deceived in this world by apparent causes. The Shaykh, the Imam, my father 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: "Were it not for the causes, no doubter would doubt." On the Day of Resurrection, the causes will vanish, the lords (*arbab*) will be deposed, and nothing will remain except the judgment of the One who causes the causes. Therefore this call is specific to the Day of Resurrection.

Know that although the apparent wording indicates that this call is specific to that Day, His saying ﴿To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ indicates that this call is in fact always in effect in meaning. This is because our saying "Allah" is a name for the Necessary Existent in Himself (*wajib al-wujud li-dhatihi*); the Necessary Existent in Himself is One, and everything other than Him is possible in itself (*mumkin li-dhatihi*). The possible in itself does not come into existence except through the bringing into being of the Necessary Existent. The meaning of bringing into being is giving preference to the side of existence over the side of non-existence, and that preference is a subjugation (*qahr*) of the disfavored side. Thus it is established that the God who is the Subduer is One forever, and the call ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾ arises only from His being One and Subduer. Since His being Subduer remains from eternity to eternity, the call ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾ remains, in terms of meaning, from eternity to eternity.

The fifth attribute of that Day is His saying: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned﴾.

* * *

Know that when He, glorified is He, had explained the attributes of subjugation on that Day, He followed them with an explanation of the attributes of justice and grace on that Day, saying: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned﴾. This contains two issues:

The first issue: this statement comprises three matters. The first is the affirmation of acquisition (*kasb*) for the human being. The second is that his acquisition necessitates recompense. The third is that this recompense is fully given on that Day. So this sentence, despite its brevity, contains these three foundations, which are highly significant in the religion. These foundations have been established many times before, but it is worth mentioning some points in establishing them.

As for the first: the affirmation of acquisition for the human being means that his limbs are sound and fit for doing and for refraining. As long as he remains in this equal state, it is impossible for doing or refraining to proceed from him. But when a motive to act or a motive to refrain is added to it, that act or refraining must proceed from him.

As for the second, which is the explanation of the consequence of recompense from it: know that actions are of two kinds. Some are motivated by seeking corporeal goods attained in the world of this life, and others are motivated by seeking spiritual goods whose full perfection appears only in the world of the Hereafter. It has been established by experience that frequent actions are a cause of the arising of firm dispositions (*malakat*). Whoever is dominated by the first kind, his desire for this world and for corporeal things becomes firmly established, so at death there occurs separation between him and what he seeks in the greatest way, and the affliction upon him becomes great. Whoever is dominated by the second kind, at death he parts from what he hated and joins with what he loves, so blessings and favors are magnified. This is the meaning of acquisition, and the meaning of that acquisition necessitating recompense. Thus it becomes clear that the full recompense is attained only on the Day of Resurrection. This is a universal rational principle, and the true Law has come with what strengthens this universal principle in the details of deeds and words. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: this verse is a great foundation in the principles of jurisprudence (*usul al-fiqh*). We say: if any kind of harm were lawfully prescribed, it would either be prescribed as a recompense for some offense or not as a recompense. Both alternatives are invalid, so the claim that it is prescribed is invalid. As for the proof that it cannot be prescribed as a recompense for some deed: this text requires the postponement of recompenses until the Day of Resurrection, so establishing it in this world would contradict this text. As for the proof that it cannot be prescribed as a recompense, [it follows] from His saying: ﴿Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], and His saying: ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ [al-Hajj: 78], and His, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: "There is no harm and no reciprocating harm in Islam." We have departed from these general statements in cases where the harms are recompenses, and in cases where a text has permitted them, such as the slaughter of animals. So it is necessary that the rest remain on the original prohibition. From what we have mentioned it is established that the basic rule concerning harms and pains is prohibition. If we find a specific text indicating legitimacy, we judge by it, giving precedence to the specific over the general. Otherwise it remains on the original prohibition. This is a universal principle, of much benefit in the Law. And Allah knows best.

The sixth attribute of that Day is His saying: ﴿There is no injustice today﴾. The purpose is that when He said: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned﴾, He followed it with something indicating that no kind of injustice occurs on that Day. The verifiers (*al-muhaqqiqun*) said: injustice in recompense occurs in four ways. The first: a person deserves a reward but is denied it. The second: one party gives another part of what is due to him but does not deliver his full right. The third: one punishes someone who does not deserve punishment. The fourth: a person deserves punishment and is punished, but is punished beyond the measure of what he deserves. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿There is no injustice today﴾ indicates the negation of these four kinds. The judge (*al-Qadi*) said: this verse is strong in refuting the view of the Jabriyya (determinists), because according to their doctrine, there is no injustice at all, either apparent or real, except from Allah. Moreover, if He creates disbelief in a person and then punishes him for it, this is the very essence of injustice. The answer to this is well known.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. The mention of this statement in this place is very fitting, because when He made clear that there is no injustice, He made clear that He is swift in reckoning. This indicates that what they deserve will reach them immediately. And Allah knows best.

[Page 38]

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs and sends down provision for you from the sky. Yet none remembers except one who turns back (to God).﴾ ﴿So call upon God, making your religion sincerely His, though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned what necessitates severe threat against the polytheists, He followed it with mention of what indicates the perfection of His power and wisdom, so that this would serve as proof that it is not permissible to make these carved stones and shaped wood partners with God, exalted is He, in worship. So He said: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs.﴾ Know that the most important of important matters is the safeguarding of the interests of religions and the interests of bodies. He, glorified and exalted is He, safeguarded the interests of the religions of His servants by manifesting the clear proofs and signs, and He safeguarded the interests of their bodies by sending down provision from the sky. Thus the place of signs with regard to religions is like the place of provisions with regard to bodies. Signs are for the life of religions, and provisions are for the life of bodies. When both are attained, favour is accomplished in the strongest of considerations and the most complete of aspects.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Yet none remembers except one who turns back (to God).﴾ The meaning is that standing upon the proofs of God's oneness is like a matter fixed in the intellect, except that affirming partnership and occupying oneself with worship of other than God becomes like a barrier against the manifestation of those lights. So when the servant turns away from these and turns back to God, exalted is He, the veil and the covering are removed, and complete success becomes apparent. When He had established this meaning, He stated the desired matter explicitly, which is turning away from other than God and fully turning toward God, exalted is He. So He said: ﴿So call upon God, making your religion sincerely His﴾ — free of polytheism and of inclination toward anything other than God. ﴿Though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ Ibn Kathir read *yunzilu* (﴿يُنَزِّلُ﴾, "He sends down") with a light (single-consonant) form, while the rest read it with the doubled form.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Exalted in degrees, Lord of the Throne, He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, that He may warn of the Day of Meeting, the Day when they will come forth, nothing of them being hidden from God. Whose is the dominion today? It is God's, the One, the Subduer.﴾ ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. There is no injustice today. Indeed God is swift in reckoning.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned among the attributes of His majesty and generosity that He manifests signs and sends down provisions, He mentioned in this verse three other attributes of majesty and greatness, which is His saying: ﴿Exalted in degrees, Lord of the Throne, He casts the Spirit.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf said: "Three predicates of His saying 'He' (huwa) are arranged upon His saying ﴿who shows you﴾, or they are predicates of an omitted subject, and they differ in definiteness and indefiniteness. It has been read *rafī'a al-darajāt* (﴿رَفِيعَ الدَّرَجاتِ﴾) in the accusative as a form of praise."

I say: It is necessary to explain these three attributes.

As for the first attribute, His saying ﴿Exalted in degrees﴾: know that *al-rafī'* may be taken to mean the one who raises, or it may be taken to mean the one who is exalted. If we take it in the first sense, there are several aspects:

The first aspect: He, exalted is He, raises the degrees of the prophets and the friends of God in Paradise.

The second: He raises the degrees of creation in knowledge and in praiseworthy character. He, glorified is He, assigned to each of the angels a specific degree, as He said: ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station﴾ [al-Saffat: 164]. He assigned to each of the scholars a specific degree, as He said: ﴿God will raise those among you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 11]. He assigned to each body a specific degree: some of them are lowly and elemental, some are stellar and astral, and some are from the substances of the Throne and the Footstool. He gave some of them a higher degree than the degree of others. Also, He assigned to each one a specific rank in creation, provision and term of life, as He said: ﴿It is He who made you successors on the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees﴾ [al-An'am: 165]. He assigned to each of the happy and the wretched in this world a specific degree of the causes of happiness and the causes of wretchedness, and in the Hereafter there are effects that manifest that happiness and wretchedness. So if we take *al-rafī'* to mean the one who raises, its meaning is what we have mentioned.

If we take it to mean the one who is exalted, then He, glorified is He, is the most exalted of existents in all attributes of perfection and majesty. As for existence itself, He is the most exalted of existents,

[Page 39]

because He is necessarily existent in Himself (wājib al-wujūd li-dhātihi), while everything other than Him is contingent (mumkin) and in need of Him. As for the permanence of existence, He is the most exalted of existents, because He is necessarily existent in Himself. He is the Eternal, the Everlasting, the Perpetual, who is the first of everything other than Him and has no first, and the last of everything other than Him and has no last. As for knowledge, He is the One who knows all essences, attributes, universals and particulars, as He said: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. As for power, He is the highest of the powerful and the most exalted of them, because in His existence and in all the perfections of His existence He is independent of everything other than Him, while everything other than Him is in need of Him in its existence and in all the perfections of its existence. As for unity, He is the One for whom it is impossible to have an opposite, a peer, a partner or an equal.

I say: The Truth, glorified is He, has two attributes. The first: His independence in His existence and in all the attributes of His existence from everything other than Him. The second: the dependence of everything other than Him upon Him in its existence and in the attributes of its existence. So *al-rafī'*, if we interpret it as "the exalted," its meaning is that He is the most exalted and highest of existents in all attributes of majesty and honour. If we interpret it as "the one who raises," its meaning is that every degree, virtue, mercy and distinction that has come to something other than Him has come only through His bringing it into existence, His originating it, His bounty and His mercy.

The second attribute: His saying ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾. Its meaning is that He is the owner of the Throne, its administrator and its creator. Some ignorant ones among the anthropomorphists (*mushabbihah*) argued with His saying ﴿Exalted in degrees, Lord of the Throne﴾, understanding by "degrees" the heavens, and by "Lord of the Throne" that He is present on the Throne above the seven heavens. They have greatly slandered God, exalted is He. We have shown by compelling rational proofs that His being a body and being in a direction is impossible. Also, the apparent wording does not indicate what they have claimed, because His saying ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾ indicates nothing more than His being related to the Throne, and to be related to it suffices by His being its owner and bringing it from non-existence into existence. So what necessity compels us to go to the false saying and the corrupt doctrine? The benefit of specifying the Throne by mention is that it is the greatest of bodies, and the aim is to show the perfection of His divinity and the penetration of His power. Whenever the locus of disposal and governance is greater, its indication of perfect power is stronger.

* * *

The third attribute: His saying ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants.﴾ Concerning it there are several discussions.

The first discussion: They differed about what is meant by this Spirit. The correct view is that what is meant is revelation (*al-wahy*). We have expanded in explaining why revelation was named "Spirit" at the beginning of Surah al-Nahl, in explaining His saying ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command﴾ [al-Nahl: 2]. He also said: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life?﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. The summary of the matter is that the life of spirits is through divine knowledge and holy manifestations. When revelation is the cause of the attainment of these spirits, it is named "Spirit," just as the spirit is the cause of attaining life, and revelation is the cause of attaining this spiritual life.

Know that this verse contains wondrous secrets from the sciences of unveilings. This is because the perfection of God's greatness cannot be reached by intellects and understandings. So the complete way of describing Him, within the human capacity, is that this statement be mentioned in its general rational form, and then something of perceptible things be mentioned after it, confirming that rational meaning, so that the description through this method supports the intellect. Here too it is like that. So His saying ﴿Exalted in degrees﴾ either means that He is raising degrees, which is an indication of the influence of God's power in bringing into existence contingent things with their differing degrees and varied ranks and attributes, or it means that He, exalted is He, is exalted in attributes of majesty and qualities of might above all existents. This statement is rational and demonstrative. Then He, glorified is He, explained this general statement with further elaboration. This is because what is other than God, exalted is He, is either corporeal things or [Page 40] spiritual things. So in this verse He explained that both kinds are subjected under the subjugation of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. As for corporeal things, the greatest of them is the Throne. So His saying ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾ indicates His dominance over the whole world of bodies. Since the Throne is of the kind of perceptible things, this perceptible thing confirms that intelligible meaning, I mean His saying ﴿Exalted in degrees﴾. As for spiritual things, all of them are subjected to the Truth, glorified is He, and to this the indication is His saying ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command.﴾

Know that the most noble of the apparent states in the spiritual beings of this world is the manifestation of the effects of revelation. Revelation is completed only by four pillars. The first of them is the Sender, who is God, glorified and exalted is He; for this reason He attributed the casting of revelation to Himself, saying ﴿He casts the Spirit.﴾ The second pillar is the sending and the revelation, which He named "the Spirit." The third pillar is that the arrival of revelation from God to the prophets is not possible except through the intermediary of the angels, and this is what is indicated in this verse by His saying ﴿by His command.﴾ So the spiritual pillar is called "command," as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command﴾ [Fussilat: 12], and He said: ﴿Surely to Him belong creation and command﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. The fourth pillar is the prophets to whom God casts revelation, and this is what is indicated by His saying ﴿upon whom He wills of His servants.﴾ The fifth pillar is the specification of the purpose and the original aim of casting this revelation to them. That is, the prophets, peace be upon them, turn people from the world of this life to the world of the Hereafter, and lead them to turn away from these bodily things and turn toward spiritual things. To this the indication is His saying ﴿that He may warn of the Day of Meeting, the Day when they will come forth.﴾ This is a wondrous arrangement that points to these lofty indications from the divine sciences of unveilings.

It remains here for us to clarify: what is the reason for calling the Day of Resurrection "the Day of Meeting," and how many attributes did God mention in this surah for the Day of Meeting?

As for the reason for calling the Day of Resurrection "the Day of Meeting," there are several views:

The first: Spirits were separated from bodies, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, spirits will meet bodies, so that day is the Day of Meeting.

The second: creatures will meet one another in it, so some of them will be informed of the state of others.

The third: the people of heaven will descend to the people of earth, so the people of heaven and the people of earth will meet on it. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And on the Day the heaven will be split open with clouds and the angels will be sent down, descending﴾ [al-Furqan: 25].

The fourth: everyone reaches the recompense of his deed on that day, and so it is from the sense of meeting, taken from the saying of people: "So-and-so met his deed."

The fifth: it may be taken from His saying: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110], and from His saying: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be "Peace"﴾ [al-Ahzab: 44].

The sixth: it is a day on which those who worship and those who are worshipped meet.

The seventh: it is a day on which Adam, peace be upon him, meets his last child.

The eighth: Maymun ibn Mihran said: it is a day on which the oppressor and the oppressed meet. A man may wrong another man and then separate from him; if he wanted to find him he would not be able to, nor recognise him. But on the Day of Resurrection they will both be present, and they will meet one another.

Ibn Kathir read (*al-talāqī wal-tanādī*, ﴿التَّلاقِي وَالتَّنادِي﴾) with the letter *yā'* affirmed both in continuation and at pause, and (*hādī* and *wāqī*, ﴿هادِي وواقِي﴾) with *yā'* at pause and with tanwin in continuation.

As for explaining how many attributes God counted and described the Day of Resurrection with in this verse, we say:

**Part 2 of 2**

The first attribute: the Day of Encounter (*yawm al-talaq*), which we have already explained.

The second attribute is His saying: ﴿the Day when they will come forth (*bariz*n*)﴾. There are several interpretations of this "coming forth":

The first: they will come forth from the depths of their graves.

The second: *bariz*n* means "manifest," that is, nothing will conceal them from a mountain, a hill, or a building, because the earth will be level and bare, a flat plain (*qa' safsaf*). Nor will they wear clothing; rather they will be naked and exposed, as has come in the hadith: "They will be gathered naked, barefoot and uncircumcised (*ghurl*)."

The third: their being manifest may be taken as a metaphor for the exposure of their deeds and the uncovering of their secrets, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿On the Day when the hidden things are tested﴾ [al-Tariq: 9].

The fourth: these rational human souls, in this world, are as if they were immersed in the darkness of the deeds of the bodies. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they turn away from occupation with managing corporeal matters and turn entirely toward the world of the Resurrection and the assembly of spiritual realities. It is as if they come forth after having been hidden within corporeal things and concealed by them.

The third attribute: His saying ﴿nothing of them is hidden from Allah﴾. The meaning is a Day on which nothing of them will be hidden from Allah, and the purpose of this is a warning. He, exalted is He, has made clear that when they come forth from their graves, gather, and meet, Allah, exalted is He, knows what each one of them has done, and He will recompense each according to his deeds: if good, then good; if evil, then evil. Even if they do not know the details of what they did, Allah, exalted is He, knows all of it. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿On that Day you will be presented, and nothing of you will be hidden﴾ [al-Haqqah: 18]. He also said: ﴿On the Day when the hidden things are tested﴾ [al-Tariq: 9], and ﴿When what is in the graves is scattered and what is in the breasts is brought out﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 9–10], and ﴿On that Day she will report her news﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 4].

If it is objected: Allah is not hidden from anything of them on all days, so what is the point of restricting this meaning to that Day? We say: In this world, when they hid behind walls and veils, they imagined that Allah did not see them and that their deeds were hidden from Him. On that Day, they pass into a state of being exposed and laid bare, in which they will not imagine what they imagined in this world. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do﴾ [Fussilat: 22], and He said: ﴿They hide from people, but they do not hide from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 108]. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾.

* * *

The fourth attribute: His exalted saying ﴿Whose is the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾. The implied sense is a Day on which it will be called out: "Whose is the dominion today?" As to when this call occurs, there are two opinions:

The first: the commentators said that when everything in the heavens and the earth has perished, the Lord, exalted is He, will say: ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection. No one will answer Him, so He answers Himself: ﴿To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾. The scholars of usul (*usul al-fiqh*, the principles of jurisprudence) said: this view is weak, and its weakness is shown in several ways:

The first: He, exalted is He, has made clear that this call takes place on the Day of Encounter, the Day of Coming Forth, and the Day when every soul is recompensed for what it earned. At that time, people are alive. So their claim that Allah calls out this call only after everything in the heavens and the earth has perished is refuted.

The second: speech must have a purpose, because speech is either uttered in the presence of another or in the absence of another. The first is invalid here, because those people say that He, exalted is He, mentions this only when all things have perished. The second is also invalid, because a person speaks in solitude either to memorize something, as one repeats a lesson, and that is impossible for Allah; or for the sake of delight in what he says, and that too is impossible for Allah; or in order to worship Allah through that remembrance, and that too is impossible for Allah. Thus it is established that the view of one who says that Allah, exalted is He, mentions this call at the time of the destruction of all creatures is false and has no basis.

The second opinion: on the Day of Encounter, when the first and the last have assembled and come forth before Allah, a caller calls out: ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾, and all who are present in the assembly of the Resurrection answer: ﴿To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾. The believers say it with delight, because by this remembrance they attain an exalted station, while the disbelievers say it in abasement and humiliation, out of regret and remorse that this remembrance escaped them in the world. Those who hold this view said: even if the first opinion is reported from Ibn 'Abbas and others, it is not impossible that the intended meaning is that this call is made after the destruction of humankind, but that there were angels present there who heard that call. I also say on this view: it is not far-fetched that the one asking and the one answering is Allah, exalted is He; nor is it far-fetched that the one asking is a group of angels and the one answering is another group. All of these are possible, and there is no definite proof for any one of them.

If it is asked: what is the benefit of restricting this call to this Day?

We say: people were deceived in this world by apparent causes. The Shaykh, the Imam, my father 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: "Were it not for the causes, no doubter would doubt." On the Day of Resurrection, the causes will vanish, the lords (*arbab*) will be deposed, and nothing will remain except the judgment of the One who causes the causes. Therefore this call is specific to the Day of Resurrection.

Know that although the apparent wording indicates that this call is specific to that Day, His saying ﴿To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ indicates that this call is in fact always in effect in meaning. This is because our saying "Allah" is a name for the Necessary Existent in Himself (*wajib al-wujud li-dhatihi*); the Necessary Existent in Himself is One, and everything other than Him is possible in itself (*mumkin li-dhatihi*). The possible in itself does not come into existence except through the bringing into being of the Necessary Existent. The meaning of bringing into being is giving preference to the side of existence over the side of non-existence, and that preference is a subjugation (*qahr*) of the disfavored side. Thus it is established that the God who is the Subduer is One forever, and the call ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾ arises only from His being One and Subduer. Since His being Subduer remains from eternity to eternity, the call ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾ remains, in terms of meaning, from eternity to eternity.

The fifth attribute of that Day is His saying: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned﴾.

* * *

Know that when He, glorified is He, had explained the attributes of subjugation on that Day, He followed them with an explanation of the attributes of justice and grace on that Day, saying: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned﴾. This contains two issues:

The first issue: this statement comprises three matters. The first is the affirmation of acquisition (*kasb*) for the human being. The second is that his acquisition necessitates recompense. The third is that this recompense is fully given on that Day. So this sentence, despite its brevity, contains these three foundations, which are highly significant in the religion. These foundations have been established many times before, but it is worth mentioning some points in establishing them.

As for the first: the affirmation of acquisition for the human being means that his limbs are sound and fit for doing and for refraining. As long as he remains in this equal state, it is impossible for doing or refraining to proceed from him. But when a motive to act or a motive to refrain is added to it, that act or refraining must proceed from him.

As for the second, which is the explanation of the consequence of recompense from it: know that actions are of two kinds. Some are motivated by seeking corporeal goods attained in the world of this life, and others are motivated by seeking spiritual goods whose full perfection appears only in the world of the Hereafter. It has been established by experience that frequent actions are a cause of the arising of firm dispositions (*malakat*). Whoever is dominated by the first kind, his desire for this world and for corporeal things becomes firmly established, so at death there occurs separation between him and what he seeks in the greatest way, and the affliction upon him becomes great. Whoever is dominated by the second kind, at death he parts from what he hated and joins with what he loves, so blessings and favors are magnified. This is the meaning of acquisition, and the meaning of that acquisition necessitating recompense. Thus it becomes clear that the full recompense is attained only on the Day of Resurrection. This is a universal rational principle, and the true Law has come with what strengthens this universal principle in the details of deeds and words. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: this verse is a great foundation in the principles of jurisprudence (*usul al-fiqh*). We say: if any kind of harm were lawfully prescribed, it would either be prescribed as a recompense for some offense or not as a recompense. Both alternatives are invalid, so the claim that it is prescribed is invalid. As for the proof that it cannot be prescribed as a recompense for some deed: this text requires the postponement of recompenses until the Day of Resurrection, so establishing it in this world would contradict this text. As for the proof that it cannot be prescribed as a recompense, [it follows] from His saying: ﴿Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], and His saying: ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ [al-Hajj: 78], and His, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: "There is no harm and no reciprocating harm in Islam." We have departed from these general statements in cases where the harms are recompenses, and in cases where a text has permitted them, such as the slaughter of animals. So it is necessary that the rest remain on the original prohibition. From what we have mentioned it is established that the basic rule concerning harms and pains is prohibition. If we find a specific text indicating legitimacy, we judge by it, giving precedence to the specific over the general. Otherwise it remains on the original prohibition. This is a universal principle, of much benefit in the Law. And Allah knows best.

The sixth attribute of that Day is His saying: ﴿There is no injustice today﴾. The purpose is that when He said: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned﴾, He followed it with something indicating that no kind of injustice occurs on that Day. The verifiers (*al-muhaqqiqun*) said: injustice in recompense occurs in four ways. The first: a person deserves a reward but is denied it. The second: one party gives another part of what is due to him but does not deliver his full right. The third: one punishes someone who does not deserve punishment. The fourth: a person deserves punishment and is punished, but is punished beyond the measure of what he deserves. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿There is no injustice today﴾ indicates the negation of these four kinds. The judge (*al-Qadi*) said: this verse is strong in refuting the view of the Jabriyya (determinists), because according to their doctrine, there is no injustice at all, either apparent or real, except from Allah. Moreover, if He creates disbelief in a person and then punishes him for it, this is the very essence of injustice. The answer to this is well known.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. The mention of this statement in this place is very fitting, because when He made clear that there is no injustice, He made clear that He is swift in reckoning. This indicates that what they deserve will reach them immediately. And Allah knows best.

[p. 44]

Allah says: ﴿And warn them of the Imminent Day, when hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief. The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor who will be obeyed.﴾ ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.﴾ ﴿And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him do not judge anything. Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾
﴿Have they not traveled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces left upon the earth, yet Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector from Allah.﴾ ﴿That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Strong, Severe in punishment.﴾

Know that the purpose of this verse is to describe the Day of Resurrection with other kinds of terrifying and awe-inspiring attributes. The verse contains several issues.

**First issue:** Scholars have mentioned several interpretations of "the Day of the Imminent" (yawm al-Azifah).

The first: The Day of the Imminent is the Day of Resurrection, and *al-Azifah* is the feminine active participle from *azifa al-amr*, meaning it drew near and arrived. This is based on His saying, describing the Day of Resurrection: ﴿The Imminent has drawn near; none besides Allah can disclose it﴾ [al-Najm: 57]. A poet said:

*The departure has drawn near, though our mounts have not yet been loaded with our baggage, and as if it had already come.*

The purpose is to alert that the Day of Resurrection is near. A parallel is His saying: ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ [al-Qamar: 1]. Al-Zajjaj said: It is called *al-Azifah* only because it is near, even if people consider its time far away, and whatever is bound to happen is near.

Know that *al-Azifah* is an adjective modifying an omitted feminine noun, as if to say: "the Day of Resurrection, the Imminent," or "the Day of Recompense, the Imminent." Al-Qaffal said: The names of the Resurrection take feminine forms, such as *al-Tammah* and *al-Haqqah* and the like, as if their meaning returns to "the calamity."

The second view: The meaning of "the Day of the Imminent" is the time of the Imminent, which is their rushing into the Fire, for at that time their hearts rise from their places out of intense fear.

The third view: Abu Muslim said: The Day of the Imminent is the day of death and the arrival of the appointed term. What indicates this is that Allah described the Day of Resurrection as the Day of Meeting, and as ﴿the Day they will emerge﴾, and then He said after it: ﴿And warn them of the Day of the Imminent﴾. Therefore this day must be other than that day. Also, this attribute is specifically applied in other verses to the day of death. He said: ﴿Why, then, when it reaches the throat, and you are at that time watching﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 83], and He said: ﴿No! When it reaches the collarbones﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 26]. Also, describing the day of death as near is more fitting than describing the Day of Resurrection as near. Also, the attributes mentioned after His saying "the Imminent" are suitable for the day of the arrival of death, because a person, upon seeing the angels of punishment, has his fear greatly increased; so it is as if their hearts reach their throats from intense fear, and they remain choking, silent about what is in their hearts of intense fear, and they will have no intimate friend nor any intercessor who removes from them the various kinds of fear and anguish.

**Second issue:** They differed over whether His saying ﴿when hearts are at the throats, choking﴾ is a metaphor for intense fear, or whether it is to be taken literally. It has been said: The intended meaning is to describe that day by intense fear and terror, and a parallel is His saying: ﴿And hearts reached the throats, and you assume about Allah assumptions﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10], and He said: ﴿Why, then, when it reaches the throat...﴾. It has also been said: Rather, it is to be taken literally. Al-Hasan said: The hearts are torn out of the breasts due to the intensity of fear, ﴿and reach the throats﴾, so they neither come out and die, nor return to their places so that they can breathe and be refreshed; rather, they are held back like a bucket in a well, as He said: ﴿When they see it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved will be distressed﴾ [al-Mulk: 27].

As for His saying ﴿choking﴾, it means distressed. *Al-kazim* is one who remains silent while filled with grief and rage. If it is asked: Why is "choking" in the accusative? We say: It is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) referring to the owners of the hearts according to the meaning, because the intended sense is: when their hearts are at their throats while they are in the state of "choking." It is also permissible for it to be a circumstantial clause referring to the hearts, meaning that the hearts are choking with grief and anguish while they reach the throats. The plural form of *al-kazimah* is the sound masculine plural, because He described them with *kazm* (choking), which is an act of rational beings, just as He said: ﴿I saw them prostrating to me﴾ [Yusuf: 4] and said: ﴿So their necks remained humbly subjected to them﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 4]. This is strengthened by the reading of those who read *kazimun*.

[p. 45]

In sum, the purpose of the verse is to establish two matters. One is intense fear, which is meant by His saying ﴿when hearts are at the throats﴾. The second is inability to speak, which is meant by His saying ﴿choking﴾. When the distressed person is able to speak, he experiences some relief and calm; but when he is unable to speak and to pour out his complaint, his anxiety becomes great and his fear grows strong.

\* \* \*

**Third issue:** Most of the Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school that denies intercession for sinners) used His saying ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor who will be obeyed﴾ to deny intercession for those who commit major sins. They said: He negated that there would be an intercessor for them who would be obeyed, so it must follow that this intercessor will not exist for them. Our companions (ashabuna) answered this in several ways.

The first: He negated that there would be an intercessor for them who is obeyed, and this does not indicate the negation of an intercessor in general. Do you not see that if you say: "I do not have a book that can be sold," this implies the negation of a sellable book, but does not imply the negation of books in general? The Arabs said:

*And you do not see the lizard entering its hole there.*

The word "obeyed" implies that the intercessor has a rank. So this indicates that on the Day of Resurrection there is no intercessor whom Allah obeys, because there is no one in existence of higher status than Allah, the Exalted, such that it could be said that Allah obeys him.

The second answer: The intended meaning of "the wrongdoers" here is the disbelievers. The evidence is that this verse was revealed to rebuke the disbelievers: ﴿those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾ [Ghafir: 35], so it must be specific to them. According to us, there is no intercession for disbelievers.

The third: The word "the wrongdoers" either denotes totality (*istighraq*) or it does not. If it denotes totality, then the intended meaning of "the wrongdoers" is their collective whole, and the disbelievers are included in this collective statement. According to us, this collective has no intercessor, because some of this collective are disbelievers and they have no intercessor; so in that case this collective has no intercessor. If it does not denote totality, then the intended meaning of "the wrongdoers" is some of those described by this attribute, and according to us, some of those described by this attribute have no intercessor, namely the disbelievers.

The proponents (the Mu'tazilah) answered the first objection, saying: The words of Allah must be interpreted in a meaningful way, and everyone knows that there is nothing in existence that Allah obeys, because the one who obeys has a lower status than the one who is obeyed, and there is nothing in existence of higher rank than Allah, the Exalted, such that it could be said that Allah obeys him. And if this meaning is known by necessity, then interpreting the verse in this way removes it from benefit. Therefore "obeyed" must be interpreted as "answered." The evidence that the word "obeyed" can mean "answered" is the saying of the poet:

*How many a man whose chest I have burned with rage, who has wished for my death but was not obeyed.*

As for the second objection, they answered it by saying that the word "wrongdoers" is a plural form preceded by the definite article, which therefore implies generality. At most, the verse was revealed to censure the disbelievers, because the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specific occasion of revelation.

As for the third objection, its answer is that His saying ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend﴾ indicates that each one of the wrongdoers is judged to have no intimate friend and no intercessor who is obeyed. This is the complete statement of the people in establishing that argument.

Our companions answered the first objection, saying: The people used to say about the idols: "They are our intercessors with Allah," and they used to say: "They will intercede for us with Allah without any need for Allah's permission." For this reason Allah refuted them by saying: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. This indicates that the people believed it was obligatory upon Allah to respond to the idols in that intercession, and this is a kind of obedience. So Allah negated that obedience by His saying: ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor who will be obeyed.﴾

[p. 46]

They answered the second statement by saying: The basic function of the definite article is to refer to a known antecedent. When the definite article is attached to a plural form and there is a previously known referent, it refers to that referent. In this verse there is a previously known referent, namely the disbelievers who dispute the signs of Allah, so it must refer to them.

They answered the third statement by saying: His saying ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor who will be obeyed﴾ may mean the negation of universal (each one is denied), or the universal negation of a collective (the collective is denied). The first, if the meaning is that each one of the wrongdoers is judged to have no intimate friend or intercessor; the second, if the meaning is that the whole collective of wrongdoers has no intimate friend or intercessor. But negating the judgment from the collective does not require negating it from each individual member of that collective. What confirms what we have mentioned is His saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, it is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 6]. If we take His saying "Indeed, those who disbelieve will not believe" to mean that each one of them is judged to not believe, then it would follow that there is a contradiction in the words of Allah, because many who disbelieved later believed. But if we take it to mean that the collective of those who disbelieve will not believe, whether some of them believe or not, it is true and free from contradiction. Therefore we interpret this verse as the negation of the totality, not as the totality of negation. Likewise, His saying ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend nor intercessor﴾ must be interpreted as the negation of totality, not as totality of negation. In that case the Mu'tazilah's use of this verse is invalid. This is the full discussion of this topic.

**Fourth issue:** Explaining the composition (*nazm*) of the verse. We say: Allah mentioned in this verse all the causes that necessitate fear. The first is that He called that day "the Day of the Imminent," that is, the day of nearness of His punishment for those who committed a great sin, because when the time of their punishment draws near, they are in the utmost extremity of fear, to the point that it is said that those griefs and anxieties are more frightening than the punishment itself.

The second is His saying ﴿when hearts are at the throats﴾, meaning that the fear reaches such a point that the heart is uprooted from the chest, rises to the throat, clings to it, and blocks the passage of breath.

The third is His saying ﴿choking﴾, meaning they are unable to speak or to express the sorrow and fear they have, and this causes greater anxiety and turmoil.

The fourth is His saying ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor who will be obeyed﴾, thus clarifying that they will have no close relative who benefits them, nor an intercessor whose intercession is obeyed on their behalf and accepted.

The fifth is His saying ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾, meaning that He, glory be to Him, is All-Knowing, from whose knowledge not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or the earth is hidden. When a judge reaches this degree of knowledge, the sinner's fear of him becomes extremely intense. The author of *al-Kashshaf* said: "Treachery" (*khaina*) is an attribute of the glance, or a verbal noun with the meaning of "treacherous," like *al-'afiyah* meaning *al-mu'afah*. The intended meaning is stealing glances at what is not lawful, as people of suspicion do. By His saying "what the breasts conceal" is meant the hidden thoughts of the hearts. The conclusion is that actions are of two kinds: actions of the limbs and actions of the hearts. As for actions of the limbs, the treachery of the eyes conceals them, and Allah knows them; so what then of the rest of the deeds?

And as for the actions of the hearts, they are known to God, Exalted, by His saying: ﴿And He knows what the breasts conceal﴾. This indicates that God, Exalted, has knowledge of all their actions.

The sixth: God's saying, Exalted: ﴿And God judges with truth﴾. This also necessitates great fear, because when a judge has knowledge of all circumstances, and it is established that he judges only with truth in everything minute and great, the fear of the sinner of him is at its utmost extent.

The seventh: the disbelievers relied, in warding off punishment from themselves, on the intercession of these idols, and God, Exalted, made clear that there is absolutely no benefit in them, so He said: ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him do not decide anything﴾.

The eighth: His saying ﴿Indeed, God is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾, meaning: He hears from the disbelievers their praise of the idols, and does not hear from them their praise of God; and He sees their prostration and submission to them, and does not see their submission
Page 47
and humility before God. So when these eight circumstances are combined regarding the sinner whose sin is great, the warning reaches the limit beyond which no further increase can be conceived. Then, when God, Exalted, had emphasized the warning to the disbelievers with the punishment of the Hereafter, He followed it with an explanation of warning them by the circumstances of this world, and He said: ﴿Have they not travelled in the land and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ The meaning is that the wise person is one who takes a lesson from others, for those who passed away from the disbelievers were stronger than these present disbelievers, and had greater traces in the land than them, meaning their fortresses, palaces and armies. When they denied their messengers, God destroyed them with various kinds of destruction, swiftly, so that these present disbelievers witness those traces, and God, Exalted, warned them against the like of that by this statement. And He explained by His saying: ﴿And they had no protector from God﴾ that when the punishment descended upon them at the time of God's seizing them, they did not find anyone to help them and deliver them. Then He explained that this descended upon them because they disbelieved and denied the messengers, so He warned the people of the Messenger against the like of it, and concluded the statement by saying that He is ﴿Mighty, severe in punishment﴾, as an intensification of warning and frightening. And God knows best.

Ibn ʿĀmir alone read "kānū hum ashadda minkum" with the kāf, while the rest read it with the hā'. As for the basis of Ibn ʿĀmir's reading, it is a shift from the third person to the second person, like His saying: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5] after His saying: ﴿Praise be to God﴾ [al-Fatiha: 1]. The reason this address is fitting is that it concerns the people of Mecca, so He made the address follow the wording of the present addressees, given their presence. This verse in meaning is like His saying: ﴿We had established them in the land as We have not established you﴾ [al-An'am: 6]. As for the reading of the rest, in the third person, it is for the sake of agreement with the third-person wording preceding it.

[p. 44]

Allah says: ﴿And warn them of the Imminent Day, when hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief. The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor who will be obeyed.﴾ ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.﴾ ﴿And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him do not judge anything. Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾
﴿Have they not traveled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces left upon the earth, yet Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector from Allah.﴾ ﴿That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Strong, Severe in punishment.﴾

Know that the purpose of this verse is to describe the Day of Resurrection with other kinds of terrifying and awe-inspiring attributes. The verse contains several issues.

**First issue:** Scholars have mentioned several interpretations of "the Day of the Imminent" (yawm al-Azifah).
