If you understand this, then in it there is complete good news: the heart's total severance from everything other than God does not occur except near death, for a person is then certain that nothing will benefit him except the grace of God, exalted is He. So according to the principle we have mentioned, supplication at that time must be accepted by God. We hope, by the grace and kindness of God, that He will grant us success in supplication joined with sincerity and humble entreaty at that time. Know that the thorough discussion of supplication has already been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: **"Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled."** That is, abased. This is a great kindness from God, exalted is He, in that He mentioned a severe threat for abandoning supplication. If it is said: it is narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said, relating from the Lord of Might, that He said: "Whoever is occupied by remembering Me from asking Me, I will give him the best of what I give to those who ask." This report implies that abandoning supplication is better, while this verse indicates that abandoning supplication entails a severe threat. How then can the two be reconciled? We say: there is no doubt that if the intellect is absorbed in praise, that is more excellent than supplication, because supplication includes knowledge of the might of lordship and the lowliness of servanthood.

Then God, exalted is He, said: **"It is God who made the night for you to rest in."** Know that its connection to what precedes it is in two ways. The first: it is as if He, exalted is He, said: I bestowed upon you before your request these great and magnificent blessings, and whoever bestowed such lofty blessings before a request, how would He not bestow lesser things after a request? The second: when He commanded supplication, it is as if it were said: occupation with supplication must necessarily be preceded by the attainment of knowledge. So what is the proof of the existence of the capable God? God, exalted is He, has mentioned these ten proofs of His existence, power and wisdom. Know that we have explained that the proofs of the existence and power of God are either celestial or elemental. As for the celestial ones, they are many kinds, the first of which is the alternation of night and day. Since most of the interests of the world are tied to these two, God, exalted is He, mentioned them in this context, and He made clear that the wisdom in creating the night is the attainment of rest through sleep and stillness, and the wisdom in creating the day is seeing things so that one may have the capacity to deal with them in the most beneficial way.

As for the fact that stillness during sleep is a cause of rest, its explanation is in two ways. The first: movements cause exhaustion, insofar as movement causes heat and dryness, and that causes pain. The second: perception of things is possible only by the delivery of the bodily spirits to the surface of the senses. Then those spirits dissolve because of the abundance of movements, so the senses and perceptions weaken. When a person sleeps, the perceptive spirits return to the inner part of the body, are settled, grow strong, and are freed from exhaustion. Also, the night is cold and moist, so its coldness and moistness compensate for what was incurred during the day of heat and dryness because of the abundance of movements. These are the known benefits from His words: **"It is God who made the night for you to rest in."**

As for His words **"and the day to see by"**: know that man is civil by nature, meaning that unless a complete city is established, the affairs of man in his food, drink, clothing and marriage are not organized. These affairs are attained only by many actions, and those actions are dealings with matters, and these dealings are not completed except by light and illumination, so that by means of that light a person distinguishes between what suits him and what does not. This is the wisdom in His words **"and the day to see by."**

If it is said: according to the requirements of the arrangement, it should have been said: "It is He who made the night for you to rest in and the day for you to see in," or "so He made the night still," but He did not say that; rather He said about the night "to rest in," and about the day "to see by." What is the benefit of this? Also, what is the wisdom in mentioning the night before the day, though the day is more noble than the night?

We say: as for the answer to the first, it is that night and sleep are, in reality, a privative nature, so it is not intended in itself, whereas wakefulness is an existential matter, and it is intended in itself. Al-Shaykh Abd al-Qahir al-Nahwi has shown in *Dala'il al-I'jaz* that the indication of the noun form for completeness and perfection is stronger than the indication of the verb form for them. So this is the reason for this difference, and God knows best.

As for the answer to the second: darkness is a privative nature, and light is an existential nature, and non-existence in created things precedes existence. For this reason He said at the beginning of Surat al-An'am: **"and made the darkness and the light"** (6:1).

Know that when God, exalted is He, mentioned what there is in the night and the day of interests and profound wisdoms, He said: **"Indeed, God is bounteous toward mankind, but most people are not grateful."** The meaning is that God's bounty toward creation is very great, but they do not thank Him. Know that abandoning thanks is for several reasons. One of them is that a man believes that these blessings are not from God, exalted is He, such as believing that these spheres necessarily exist by their own essence and necessarily revolve by their own essence. In that case, this man does not believe that these blessings are from God. The second is that a man, although he believes that the whole world came into being by God's creation and bringing into existence, yet when such great blessings, namely the blessing of the succession of night and day, have persisted and continued, man forgets them. Then when a person is afflicted with the loss of some of them, he recognizes their worth. For example, it may happen to some people, God forbid, that some oppressors imprison them in deep dark wells for a long time. Then that person recognizes the worth of the blessing of clean air and the worth of the blessing of light. I have seen some kings who tormented some of their servants by ordering people to prevent him from leaning against a wall and from sleeping, and the effect of this torment was great.

The third is that a man, although he is aware of the places of these blessings, is greedy for this world and loves wealth and rank. When abundant wealth and wide rank escape him, he falls into ingratitude for these great blessings. Since most of creation are perishing in one of these three valleys that we have mentioned, for this reason God, exalted is He, said: **"but most people are not grateful."** A parallel to this is His words: **"And few of My servants are grateful"** (34:13), and Iblis's saying: **"and You will not find most of them grateful"** (7:17). When God, exalted is He, by these mentioned proofs, made clear the existence of the capable, merciful, wise God, He said: **"That is God, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no god but He."** The author of *al-Kashshaf* said: "That" refers to the known one, distinguished by the particular acts in which no one shares with Him. And "God, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no god but He" are successive predicates, meaning: He is the one who combines these attributes of divinity and lordship, the creation of all things, and that He has no second. **"So how are you deluded?"** The meaning is: how are you turned away, and why do you deviate from these proofs and deny them? Then God, exalted is He, said: **"Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of God."** (40:63) That is, everyone who denies the signs of God and does not reflect upon them, and has no resolve to seek the truth and fear the consequence, is deluded just as they were deluded.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 40, verse 64–67:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is Allah who made the earth a resting-place for you and the sky a canopy, and fashioned you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿He is the Living; there is no god but He. So call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His. Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿Say: Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides Allah, since the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿He is the One who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then brings you forth as a child, then that you may reach your maturity, then that you may become elders—though some of you are taken before that—and that you may reach a specified term, and perhaps you will use reason.﴾

Know that we have explained that the proofs of the existence of Allah and His power are either among the proofs of the horizons (al-afaq) or among the proofs of the souls (al-anfus). As for the proofs of the horizons, what is meant is everything other than man in this whole world, and they are many kinds. What is mentioned of them in this verse includes the states of night and day, and this has already been mentioned.

Second: the earth and the sky, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿It is Allah who made the earth a resting-place for you and the sky a canopy.﴾ Ibn Abbas said regarding His saying ﴿a resting-place﴾: that is, a dwelling during life and after death. ﴿And the sky a canopy﴾ like a dome raised over the earth. It was also said: He held the earth without pillars until it became possible to act upon it. ﴿And the sky a canopy﴾: that is, standing firm and fixed, for otherwise it would fall upon us.

As for the proofs of the souls, what is meant by them is the indication of the states of the human body and the indication of the states of his self upon the existence of the Creator, the Powerful, the Wise. What is mentioned of them in this verse consists of two kinds: the first is what is present and observed in the state of his full perfection, and the second is what existed at the beginning of his creation and formation.

As for the first kind: it has many types, and what is mentioned of them in this verse are three types. The first is the coming into being of his form, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿and fashioned you﴾. The second is the beauty of his form, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿and perfected your forms﴾. The third is that He provided him with good things, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿and provided you with good things﴾. We have elaborated on these matters in this book many times, especially in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have honoured the children of Adam﴾ [al-Isra: 70].

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned these five proofs—two from the proofs of the horizons and three from the proofs of the souls—He said: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ The explanation of "tabaraka" is either permanence and stability, or abundance of good. Then He said: ﴿He is the Living; there is no god but He.﴾ This indicates restriction, that there is no living one except Him. Therefore it is necessary to understand this as the Living who is impossible to die by an essential impossibility; and then there is no living one except Him, so it is as if He treats whatever may cease to exist as if it were non-existent.

Know that "the Living" is an expression for the Perceiver, the Active. "Perceiver" points to complete knowledge, and "Active" points to complete power. When He drew attention to these two attributes among the attributes of majesty, He drew attention to the third attribute, which is oneness, by His saying: "there is no god but He." When He described Himself with these attributes, He commanded the servants with two things:

The first is calling upon Him (du'a'), and the second is sincerity in it. So He said: ﴿So call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His.﴾ Then He said: ﴿Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ It may be that what is meant is the saying "Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds." And it may be that what is meant is that since He is described by the attributes of majesty and might, He deserves in His essence that it be said to Him: "Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds." When He had made clear the attributes of majesty and greatness, He said: ﴿Say: Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides Allah.﴾ Thus He presented this to the polytheists in the gentlest manner, so as to turn them away from worshipping idols, and He made clear that the reason for the prohibition is what came to him of clear proofs. Those clear proofs are that the God of the world has been established as having the attributes of majesty and greatness, as mentioned earlier, and that pure reason testifies that worship is fitting only for Him, and that making carved stones and fashioned wood partners with Him in lordship is repugnant to the immediate judgment of reason.

When He made clear that He had commanded the worship of Allah, exalted is He, He said: ﴿and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.﴾ He mentioned these rulings concerning Himself only because they used to believe about him that he was at the utmost of intellect and perfection of substance. And it is known by necessity that every person does not desire for himself except what is best and most complete. So when he mentions that his welfare is not completed except by turning away from other than Allah and turning wholly to obedience to Allah, it becomes clear that this path is more complete than everything else. Then He said: ﴿He is the One who created you from dust.﴾

Know that we have mentioned that the proofs are of two kinds: the proofs of the horizons and of the souls. As for the proofs of the horizons, they are many, and what is mentioned of them in this verse are four: the night, the day, the earth, and the sky.

As for the proofs of the souls, we have mentioned that they are of two kinds. The first is the states present in the condition of full health, which are many kinds, and what is mentioned here of them are three types: the form, the beauty of the form, and the provision of good things.

As for the second kind, which is the manner of the coming into being of this body from the beginning of its existence as a drop, and an embryo, until the end of old age and death, this is what is mentioned in this verse when He said: ﴿He is the One who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen.﴾ It was said: what is meant is Adam. In my view there is no need for this, because every human being is created from semen and from the blood of menstruation, and semen is created from blood. Man is created from blood, and blood is only generated from foods, and foods are either animal or plant. The situation in the generation of that animal is like the situation in the generation of a human being. So all foods ultimately trace back to plant foods, and the plant comes only from the dust, becoming a drop, then a clot; after being a clot there are many stages until it is separated from the mother's womb. Allah, exalted is He, left out mentioning these stages here because He mentioned them in the other verses.

Know that Allah, exalted is He, arranged the lifespan of man into three stages. The first is his being a child; the second is that he reaches his full strength (ashuddahu); and the third is old age. This is a sound arrangement, agreeing with reason; for man in the beginning of his life is in growth, development, and increase, and this is called childhood.

The second stage is that he reaches the completion of growth and the full strength of age without any kind of weakness or deficiency having entered him, and this stage is what is meant by His saying ﴿then that you may become elders﴾. When you know this division, you know that the stages of life according to this division do not exceed these three.

The author of al-Kashshaf said: His saying ﴿that you may reach your full strength﴾ is connected to a verb omitted, whose estimate is: "then He leaves you alive so that you may reach..."

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and some of you are taken before that﴾: that is, before old age, or before these states, if one comes out as a miscarriage.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and that you may reach a specified term﴾: its meaning is that He does this so that you may reach a specified term, which is the time of death. It was also said it is the Day of Resurrection.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and perhaps you will use reason﴾: regarding what is in these wondrous states of kinds of lessons and categories of proofs.

As for the second kind, which is the manner of the coming into being of this body from the beginning of its existence as a drop, and an embryo, until the end of old age and death, this is what is mentioned in this verse when He said: ﴿He is the One who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen.﴾ It was said: what is meant is Adam. In my view there is no need for this, because every human being is created from semen and from the blood of menstruation, and semen is created from blood. Man is created from blood, and blood is only generated from foods, and foods are either animal or plant. The situation in the generation of that animal is like the situation in the generation of a human being. So all foods ultimately trace back to plant foods, and the plant comes only from the dust, becoming a drop, then a clot; after being a clot there are many stages until it is separated from the mother's womb. Allah, exalted is He, left out mentioning these stages here because He mentioned them in the other verses.

Know that Allah, exalted is He, arranged the lifespan of man into three stages. The first is his being a child; the second is that he reaches his full strength (ashuddahu); and the third is old age. This is a sound arrangement, agreeing with reason; for man in the beginning of his life is in growth, development, and increase, and this is called childhood.

The second stage is that he reaches the completion of growth and the full strength of age without any kind of weakness or deficiency having entered him, and this stage is what is meant by His saying ﴿then that you may become elders﴾. When you know this division, you know that the stages of life according to this division do not exceed these three.

The author of al-Kashshaf said: His saying ﴿that you may reach your full strength﴾ is connected to a verb omitted, whose estimate is: "then He leaves you alive so that you may reach..."

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and some of you are taken before that﴾: that is, before old age, or before these states, if one comes out as a miscarriage.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and that you may reach a specified term﴾: its meaning is that He does this so that you may reach a specified term, which is the time of death. It was also said it is the Day of Resurrection.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and perhaps you will use reason﴾: regarding what is in these wondrous states of kinds of lessons and categories of proofs.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 40, verse 64–67:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is Allah who made the earth a resting-place for you and the sky a canopy, and fashioned you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿He is the Living; there is no god but He. So call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His. Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿Say: Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides Allah, since the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿He is the One who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then brings you forth as a child, then that you may reach your maturity, then that you may become elders—though some of you are taken before that—and that you may reach a specified term, and perhaps you will use reason.﴾

Know that we have explained that the proofs of the existence of Allah and His power are either among the proofs of the horizons (al-afaq) or among the proofs of the souls (al-anfus). As for the proofs of the horizons, what is meant is everything other than man in this whole world, and they are many kinds. What is mentioned of them in this verse includes the states of night and day, and this has already been mentioned.

Second: the earth and the sky, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿It is Allah who made the earth a resting-place for you and the sky a canopy.﴾ Ibn Abbas said regarding His saying ﴿a resting-place﴾: that is, a dwelling during life and after death. ﴿And the sky a canopy﴾ like a dome raised over the earth. It was also said: He held the earth without pillars until it became possible to act upon it. ﴿And the sky a canopy﴾: that is, standing firm and fixed, for otherwise it would fall upon us.

As for the proofs of the souls, what is meant by them is the indication of the states of the human body and the indication of the states of his self upon the existence of the Creator, the Powerful, the Wise. What is mentioned of them in this verse consists of two kinds: the first is what is present and observed in the state of his full perfection, and the second is what existed at the beginning of his creation and formation.

As for the first kind: it has many types, and what is mentioned of them in this verse are three types. The first is the coming into being of his form, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿and fashioned you﴾. The second is the beauty of his form, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿and perfected your forms﴾. The third is that He provided him with good things, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿and provided you with good things﴾. We have elaborated on these matters in this book many times, especially in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have honoured the children of Adam﴾ [al-Isra: 70].

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned these five proofs—two from the proofs of the horizons and three from the proofs of the souls—He said: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ The explanation of "tabaraka" is either permanence and stability, or abundance of good. Then He said: ﴿He is the Living; there is no god but He.﴾ This indicates restriction, that there is no living one except Him. Therefore it is necessary to understand this as the Living who is impossible to die by an essential impossibility; and then there is no living one except Him, so it is as if He treats whatever may cease to exist as if it were non-existent.

Know that "the Living" is an expression for the Perceiver, the Active. "Perceiver" points to complete knowledge, and "Active" points to complete power. When He drew attention to these two attributes among the attributes of majesty, He drew attention to the third attribute, which is oneness, by His saying: "there is no god but He." When He described Himself with these attributes, He commanded the servants with two things:

The first is calling upon Him (du'a'), and the second is sincerity in it. So He said: ﴿So call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His.﴾ Then He said: ﴿Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ It may be that what is meant is the saying "Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds." And it may be that what is meant is that since He is described by the attributes of majesty and might, He deserves in His essence that it be said to Him: "Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds." When He had made clear the attributes of majesty and greatness, He said: ﴿Say: Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides Allah.﴾ Thus He presented this to the polytheists in the gentlest manner, so as to turn them away from worshipping idols, and He made clear that the reason for the prohibition is what came to him of clear proofs. Those clear proofs are that the God of the world has been established as having the attributes of majesty and greatness, as mentioned earlier, and that pure reason testifies that worship is fitting only for Him, and that making carved stones and fashioned wood partners with Him in lordship is repugnant to the immediate judgment of reason.

When He made clear that He had commanded the worship of Allah, exalted is He, He said: ﴿and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.﴾ He mentioned these rulings concerning Himself only because they used to believe about him that he was at the utmost of intellect and perfection of substance. And it is known by necessity that every person does not desire for himself except what is best and most complete. So when he mentions that his welfare is not completed except by turning away from other than Allah and turning wholly to obedience to Allah, it becomes clear that this path is more complete than everything else. Then He said: ﴿He is the One who created you from dust.﴾

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 40, verse 68:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He is the One who gives life and causes death. So when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned the human being's transition from being dust to being a drop (nutfah), then to being a clinging clot ('alaqah), then to being an infant, then to reaching maturity (bulugh al-ashudd), then to old age, and He cited these changes as evidence for the existence of the All-Powerful God, He said after it: ﴿He is the One who gives life and causes death.﴾ That is, just as the transition from one attribute to another of the attributes mentioned earlier indicates an All-Powerful God, so too the transition from life to death and the reverse indicates an All-Powerful God. And His saying ﴿So when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ has several aspects:

The first: its meaning is that when He moves these bodies from some of these attributes to another attribute, He does not tire in that action and does not need an instrument or tool. So He expressed the penetration of His power over existing things and created things, without any opponent or resister, by saying: ("Be," and it is).

The second aspect: He expressed giving life and causing death by the saying ﴿"Be," and it is.﴾ It is as if it were said: the transition from being dust to being a drop, then to being a clot, are transitions that occur gradually, little by little; but the coming into being of life occurs only through the attachment of the substance of the rational soul to it, and that happens in a single instant. For this reason it was expressed by His saying ﴿"Be," and it is.﴾

The third aspect: some people say that the formation of a human being is only established from semen and blood in the womb within a specific period and according to its transitions from state to state. So it is as if it were said: it is impossible that every human being should come from another human being, because an infinite regress is impossible, and the occurrence of a created thing in eternity is impossible. Therefore it is necessary to acknowledge a human being who is the first of mankind. Then the coming into being of that human being is not through semen and blood, but through God, exalted is He, originating him directly. God, exalted is He, expressed this meaning by His saying ﴿"Be," and it is.﴾

Al-Razi, *Mafatih al-Ghayb*, on Surah 40, verses 69–76:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah? How are they turned away?﴾ ﴿Those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers. But they will come to know,﴾ ﴿when the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged,﴾ ﴿through the scalding water, then in the Fire they are burned.﴾ ﴿Then it will be said to them: "Where are those you used to associate,﴾ ﴿besides Allah?" They will say: "They have gone astray from us. Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before." Thus Allah leads the disbelievers astray.﴾ ﴿That is because you used to exult in the earth without right, and because you used to be insolent.﴾ ﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant.﴾

Know that He, may He be exalted, returned to censuring those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, so He said: ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah? How are they turned away?﴾ This is a censure of them for disputing the signs of Allah, repelling them, and denying them. Thus He, may He be exalted, expressed wonder at them with His saying ﴿How are they turned away?﴾, as a man says to one who does not make clear [his position]: "Where are you being taken?", expressing amazement at his heedlessness. Then He explained that they are ﴿those who denied the Book﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿and what We sent with Our messengers﴾ of the other books.

If it is said: *sawfa* (سوف) refers to the future, and *idh* (إذ) refers to the past, so His saying ﴿but they will come to know﴾ ﴿when the shackles are around their necks﴾ is like your saying: "I will fast yesterday." We say: what is meant by His saying *idh* (إذ) is *idha* (إذا, "when"). Since future matters, in Allah's report, are certain and definite, He expressed them with the wording of what has occurred and been realized, while the meaning is future. This is the wording of the author of *al-Kashshaf*.

Then He described the manner of their punishment, saying: ﴿when the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged﴾ ﴿through the scalding water﴾. The meaning is that there will be shackles and chains around their necks, then they will be dragged with those chains through the scalding water, that is, the water heated by the fire of Hell. ﴿Then in the Fire they are burned.﴾ *Sajr* (السجر), linguistically, means kindling in an oven, and its meaning is that they are in the Fire, which encompasses them. Close to this is His saying: ﴿the fire of Allah, kindled, which mounts over the hearts﴾ [al-Humazah: 6–7].

﴿Then it will be said to them: "Where are those you used to associate﴾ ﴿besides Allah?"﴾ They will say: ﴿"They have gone astray from us,"﴾ that is, they vanished from our sight, so we do not see them and do not seek their intercession. Then they said: ﴿"Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before,"﴾ that is, it has become clear that they were nothing, and that by worshipping them we were not worshipping anything, as you say: "I thought that so-and-so was something, but when you test him you find no good in him, and he is nothing." It is also permissible to say that they denied and disavowed having worshipped other than Allah, as Allah, may He be exalted, reported about them in Surah al-An'am, that they said: ﴿"By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾ [al-An'am: 23].

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Thus Allah leads the disbelievers astray.﴾ The judge (al-Qadi) said: its meaning is that He leads them astray from the path to Paradise, since it is not permissible to say that He leads them astray from the proof, for He had already guided them to it in this world. The author of *al-Kashshaf* said: ﴿Thus Allah leads the disbelievers astray﴾ is like the straying of their gods from them; He leads them astray from their gods, so that if they sought the gods, or if you sought the gods, neither of the two would find the other. Then He said: ﴿That is because you used to exult in the earth﴾, that is, that misguidance is because of what you had of exultation and insolence without right, which is polytheism and the worship of idols. ﴿Enter the gates of Hell﴾, the seven gates allotted to you. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿It has seven gates; for each gate there is a designated portion of them﴾ [al-Hijr: 44]. ﴿Abiding therein. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant.﴾

[Page 77]

What is meant by this is what He said in the previous verse concerning the description of these disputers: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but pride﴾ [Ghafir: 56].

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 40, verses 77–78:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And whether We show you part of what We promise them or We take you in death, to Us they will be returned.﴾ ﴿And We had already sent messengers before you; among them are those We have related to you and among them are those We have not related to you. And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah. So when the command of Allah comes, it will be concluded in truth, and the falsifiers will lose therein.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, had spoken from the beginning of the surah up to this point, refuting the method of those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, He commanded His Messenger in this verse to be patient in the face of their harm and their alienation through those disputes. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true.﴾ By this He meant what He promised the Messenger of support and of sending punishment upon his enemies. Then He said: ﴿And whether We show you part of what We promise them﴾, meaning those disbelievers, of the kinds of punishment, such as killing on the day of Badr; that is what is sought. ﴿Or We take you in death﴾ before the punishment is sent down upon them. ﴿To Us they will be returned﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, and We will take vengeance upon them with the utmost vengeance. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whether We take you away, indeed We will take vengeance upon them. Or We show you that which We promised them, for indeed We are Omnipotent over them.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 41].

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We had already sent messengers before you; among them are those We have related to you and among them are those We have not related to you.﴾ The meaning is that He said to Muhammad (ﷺ): You are like the messengers before you. We have mentioned the condition of some of them to you, and We have not mentioned the condition of the rest. There was none among them to whom Allah gave signs and miracles except that his people disputed with him concerning them and denied him concerning them, and there befell them of distress what approximates what befell you, so they were patient. They would always propose to the prophets the manifestation of miracles beyond what was needed, by way of obstinacy and stubbornness. Then, when Allah, exalted is He, knew that the benefit lay in manifesting what He manifested, and otherwise He would not have manifested it, and that doing so would not have been detrimental to their prophethood, the same holds regarding your people's proposal to you of miracles beyond what is needed: since manifesting them was not beneficial, We certainly did not manifest them. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah.﴾ Then He said: ﴿So when the command of Allah comes, it will be concluded in truth.﴾ This is a warning that came following the proposal of signs. "The command of Allah" is the Resurrection, and "the falsifiers" are the obstinate ones who dispute concerning the signs of Allah and propose miracles beyond what is needed, by way of stubbornness.

Know that when He, exalted is He, had elaborated at length on establishing the threat, He returned to mentioning what indicates the existence of the Wise, Merciful God, and to mentioning what may be counted as a blessing upon the servants. Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 40, verses 82–85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them, and greater in strength and in traces left upon the earth; yet what they used to earn did not avail them.﴾ ﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they exulted in what knowledge they had; and there encompassed them that which they used to mock.﴾ ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ ﴿But their faith was not going to benefit them when they saw Our might. This is the way of Allah that has passed among His servants. And there the disbelievers were lost.﴾

Know that He, exalted is He, observed a subtle arrangement at the end of this surah. He mentioned a section on the proofs of divinity, the perfection of power, mercy and wisdom, and then followed it with the section of threat and warning. The section on which this surah concludes is the one containing the warning. The point is that these disbelievers who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, and in whose breasts great arrogance has arisen, do so for this reason, and the cause of all of it is the pursuit of leadership and of precedence over others in wealth and status.

Whoever abandons submission to the truth for the sake of pursuing these things has sold the Hereafter for the world. Thus He, exalted is He, made clear that this way is corrupt, because the world is transient and passing away. He argued against this with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ That is, if they had travelled through the regions of the earth, they would have known that the end of the arrogant and rebellious is nothing but destruction and perdition, even though they were more numerous in count, wealth and status than these later ones. Since they gained from that great power and dominant dominion nothing but failure, loss, regret and ruin, how then would be the condition of these poor, humble people?

As for the proof that they were more numerous than these, it is known only from reports. As for their being greater in strength and in traces upon the earth, that is because their traces remain after them in great fortresses, such as the pyramids present in Egypt, and such as those great cities which the earlier kings built, and such as what Allah related about them, that they used to hew houses out of the mountains.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿yet what they used to earn did not avail them.﴾ The mā in His saying ﴿fa-mā aghnā ʿanhum﴾ is either negative or implies the meaning of interrogation, and its place is in the accusative. The mā in His saying ﴿mā kānū yaksibūn﴾ is either a relative pronoun or a verbal-noun (maṣdariyyah), and its place is in the nominative. The meaning is: what thing did what they acquired, or their earning, avail them?

Then He, exalted is He, made clear that those disbelievers, when their messengers came to them with clear proofs and miracles, exulted in the knowledge they had. Know that the pronoun in His saying ﴿fariḥū﴾ (they exulted) may refer to the disbelievers, or it may refer to the messengers. If we say it refers to the disbelievers, then what knowledge was it that they exulted in? There are several views on this:

The first: that what is meant is the things they used to call knowledge, namely the doubts which Allah related of them in the Qur'an, such as their saying ﴿Nothing destroys us except time﴾ [al-Jāthiyah: 24], and their saying ﴿Had Allah willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers﴾ [al-An'ām: 148], and their saying ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 78], and ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾ [al-Kahf: 36]. They used to rejoice in this and repel by it the knowledge of the prophets, as He said: ﴿Every faction, in what they have, rejoices﴾ [al-Rūm: 32].

The second: it is possible that what is meant is the sciences of the philosophers, for when they heard of the revelation of Allah they repelled it and belittled the knowledge of the prophets in comparison with their own sciences. It is related of Socrates that he heard of the coming of some prophets, and it was said to him: "If only you would emigrate," and he said: "We are a people who are guided, so there is no need for us for one who guides us."

The third: it is possible that what is meant is their knowledge of worldly affairs and their understanding of managing them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They know an outward aspect of the worldly life, while they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾ [al-Rūm: 7], and ﴿That is the extent of their knowledge﴾ [al-Najm: 30]. When the messengers came to them with the sciences of religion, which are the knowledge of Allah, the knowledge of the servant's duties, and the purification of the soul from vices, they paid no heed to them and mocked them, and they believed that there is no knowledge more beneficial or more productive of advantages than their own knowledge, so they exulted in it.

As for if we say the pronoun refers to the prophets, then there are two views:

The first: that the exultation is attributed to the messengers, and its meaning is that when the messengers saw from their people complete ignorance and aversion from the truth, and knew the evil of their end and the punishment that would befall them for their ignorance and aversion, they rejoiced in what they had been given of knowledge and thanked Allah for it, and there befell the disbelievers the recompense of their ignorance and mockery. The second: that what is meant is that they exulted in what the messengers had of knowledge, with the exultation of laughing at it and mocking it, as if He said: they mocked the clear proofs and what they brought of the knowledge of revelation, exulting, and His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And there befell them that which they used to mock﴾ indicates this.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ Al-ba's is the severity of the punishment, and from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿with a severe punishment﴾ [al-A'rāf: 165]. If it is asked: what is the difference between His saying ﴿But their faith was not going to benefit them﴾ and what would be said if it were said "fa-lam yanfaʿhum īmānuhum"? We say: it is like kāna in such sayings as His ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son﴾ [Maryam: 35], and the meaning is: it was not valid nor proper that their faith should benefit them. If it is asked: mention a rule regarding the time at which bringing faith does not benefit, we say: it is the time at which one witnesses the descent of the angels of mercy and of punishment, for at that time a person becomes compelled to faith, and that faith does not benefit, for it benefits only together with the capacity to do otherwise, so that the person is one who chooses. But when they witness the signs of the Hereafter, then it does not.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿This is the way of Allah that has passed among His servants.﴾ The meaning is that the non-acceptance of faith at the moment of despair is a constant way of Allah among all nations.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And there the disbelievers were lost.﴾ His saying ﴿hunālika﴾ (there) is used metaphorically for time, that is: they lost at the time of seeing the might. And Allah is the Guide to what is right.

The commentary on this surah was completed on Saturday, the second of Dhu al-Hijjah, in the year six hundred and three of the Hijrah, in the town of Herat.

O You, whose lowest share of Your majesty and might is not reached by the highest descriptions of those who describe You; O You, from whose encompassing the first principles of the secrets of Your greatness the understandings of those who reflect and the gazes of those who contemplate fall short, do not place us, by Your grace and mercy, among the losers, the falsifiers; and do not make us on the Day of Resurrection among the deprived, for You are the most generous of the generous.

And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may the blessings of Allah be upon our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and his family and all his companions.

It is related of Socrates that he heard of the coming of some prophets, and it was said to him: "If only you would emigrate," and he said: "We are a people who are guided, so there is no need for us for one who guides us."

The third: it is possible that what is meant is their knowledge of worldly affairs and their understanding of managing them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They know an outward aspect of the worldly life, while they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾ [al-Rūm: 7], and ﴿That is the extent of their knowledge﴾ [al-Najm: 30]. When the messengers came to them with the sciences of religion, which are the knowledge of Allah, the knowledge of the servant's duties, and the purification of the soul from vices, they paid no heed to them and mocked them, and they believed that there is no knowledge more beneficial or more productive of advantages than their own knowledge, so they exulted in it.

As for if we say the pronoun refers to the prophets, then there are two views:

The first: that the exultation is attributed to the messengers, and its meaning is that when the messengers saw from their people complete ignorance and aversion from the truth, and knew the evil of their end and the punishment that would befall them for their ignorance and aversion, they rejoiced in what they had been given of knowledge and thanked Allah for it, and there befell the disbelievers the recompense of their ignorance and mockery. The second: that what is meant is that they exulted in what the messengers had of knowledge, with the exultation of laughing at it and mocking it, as if He said: they mocked the clear proofs and what they brought of the knowledge of revelation, exulting, and His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And there befell them that which they used to mock﴾ indicates this.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ Al-ba's is the severity of the punishment, and from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿with a severe punishment﴾ [al-A'rāf: 165]. If it is asked: what is the difference between His saying ﴿But their faith was not going to benefit them﴾ and what would be said if it were said "fa-lam yanfaʿhum īmānuhum"? We say: it is like kāna in such sayings as His ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son﴾ [Maryam: 35], and the meaning is: it was not valid nor proper that their faith should benefit them. If it is asked: mention a rule regarding the time at which bringing faith does not benefit, we say: it is the time at which one witnesses the descent of the angels of mercy and of punishment, for at that time a person becomes compelled to faith, and that faith does not benefit, for it benefits only together with the capacity to do otherwise, so that the person is one who chooses. But when they witness the signs of the Hereafter, then it does not.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿This is the way of Allah that has passed among His servants.﴾ The meaning is that the non-acceptance of faith at the moment of despair is a constant way of Allah among all nations.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And there the disbelievers were lost.﴾ His saying ﴿hunālika﴾ (there) is used metaphorically for time, that is: they lost at the time of seeing the might. And Allah is the Guide to what is right.

The commentary on this surah was completed on Saturday, the second of Dhu al-Hijjah, in the year six hundred and three of the Hijrah, in the town of Herat.

O You, whose lowest share of Your majesty and might is not reached by the highest descriptions of those who describe You; O You, from whose encompassing the first principles of the secrets of Your greatness the understandings of those who reflect and the gazes of those who contemplate fall short, do not place us, by Your grace and mercy, among the losers, the falsifiers; and do not make us on the Day of Resurrection among the deprived, for You are the most generous of the generous.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 40, verses 82–85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them, and greater in strength and in traces left upon the earth; yet what they used to earn did not avail them.﴾ ﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they exulted in what knowledge they had; and there encompassed them that which they used to mock.﴾ ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ ﴿But their faith was not going to benefit them when they saw Our might. This is the way of Allah that has passed among His servants. And there the disbelievers were lost.﴾

Know that He, exalted is He, observed a subtle arrangement at the end of this surah. He mentioned a section on the proofs of divinity, the perfection of power, mercy and wisdom, and then followed it with the section of threat and warning. The section on which this surah concludes is the one containing the warning. The point is that these disbelievers who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, and in whose breasts great arrogance has arisen, do so for this reason, and the cause of all of it is the pursuit of leadership and of precedence over others in wealth and status.

Whoever abandons submission to the truth for the sake of pursuing these things has sold the Hereafter for the world. Thus He, exalted is He, made clear that this way is corrupt, because the world is transient and passing away. He argued against this with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ That is, if they had travelled through the regions of the earth, they would have known that the end of the arrogant and rebellious is nothing but destruction and perdition, even though they were more numerous in count, wealth and status than these later ones. Since they gained from that great power and dominant dominion nothing but failure, loss, regret and ruin, how then would be the condition of these poor, humble people?

As for the proof that they were more numerous than these, it is known only from reports. As for their being greater in strength and in traces upon the earth, that is because their traces remain after them in great fortresses, such as the pyramids present in Egypt, and such as those great cities which the earlier kings built, and such as what Allah related about them, that they used to hew houses out of the mountains.
